2120.pullQuote: Book this Denny Triangle dining room when someone else is picking up the check.
2120.blurb: Save 2120 for the night someone else is hosting. The cooking is New American, the room is dressed for a celebration, and Denny Triangle is simply where the table happens to be.

1988-cocktail-lounge.pullQuote: Georgetown night owls should keep this cocktail lounge in their back pocket.
1988-cocktail-lounge.blurb: Late-night drinkers in Georgetown land at 1988 Cocktail Lounge for mixed drinks that keep coming well after eleven.

a-k-pizza.pullQuote: Charred, crackly crust and a cloud of chew make this the city's pizza to beat.
a-k-pizza.blurb: Getting your hands on a pie from A.K. Pizza takes real effort, but the crust that shatters outside and tears open into airy fluff makes it worth every bit. Go for the scamorza and vodka sauce pie or a plain cheese, then grab one of the enormous salted chocolate cookies on the way out.

aa-sushi.pullQuote: Excellent nigiri at casual prices, and you can usually walk right in with friends.
aa-sushi.blurb: AA Sushi in Ballard makes a casual sushi night feel like a splurge without the bill. Small groups can usually stroll in and sit down fast in a plain but comfortable room. Cover the table in nigiri, rolls, and miso soup, and pay attention to the rice, which holds together and stays just warm enough to soften a slice of yellowtail belly.

ada-s-restaurant-bar.pullQuote: Bring the parents here for a Turkish dinner that feels like an occasion.
ada-s-restaurant-bar.blurb: For a dressed-up Turkish meal in Phinney Ridge, Ada's Restaurant & Bar carries a special-occasion check that works well with family in tow.

afternoon-tea-at-fairmont-olympic-hotel.pullQuote: Claim a stool along the round center bar and play hotel guest for an evening.
afternoon-tea-at-fairmont-olympic-hotel.blurb: Afternoon Tea at Fairmont Olympic Hotel sits inside one of downtown's grandest old lobbies, where it's easy to pretend you have a room upstairs. Skip the hidden speakeasy and take a stool at the circular counter at the center of the room. The cocktails hold up well, with pairings like cognac and orgeat or tequila with chocolate bitters.

aladdin-gyro-cery.pullQuote: Skip the other falafel joints near campus and come straight here.
aladdin-gyro-cery.blurb: Of all the falafel options around the University District, Aladdin Gyro-Cery should stay on your list. The falafel comes out shatteringly crisp, and the tahini sauce is good enough to sip. Orders move fast for takeout, though you can also settle into the couches in back with feta fries.

alebrijes-kitchen.pullQuote: A sleepy little dining room turning out seriously great Mexican food.
alebrijes-kitchen.blurb: The room at Alebrijes Kitchen is quiet, with only a few tables, but the kitchen is anything but. Tortilla-wrapped dishes fly out at a steady clip and can rescue the dullest weeknight. Start with the fiery orange salsa and build from there.

alibi-room.pullQuote: Pizza down Post Alley, past the gum wall and steps from the Market.
alibi-room.blurb: Alibi Room is a pizza bar down Post Alley, past the gum wall and steps from the Market. Well drinks and house cocktails are poured here too, including a sazerac sweetened with brown sugar and rosemary, and there is spicy mac and cheese.

alki-spud-fish-and-chips.pullQuote: Pay the extra few bucks for halibut and eat it near the beach.
alki-spud-fish-and-chips.blurb: Alki Spud Fish and Chips has been frying seafood by the beach since the thirties, and old photos and maps of West Seattle cover the walls to prove it. The halibut costs a little more and is absolutely the order, flaky and tender under a crisp, well-seasoned batter. Portions can run huge, and it all comes cheap enough when midday has to be fast or a visit with out-of-town guests.

altitude-sky-lounge.pullQuote: Take visitors up here for skyline cocktails that last past eleven.
altitude-sky-lounge.blurb: Up on a South Lake Union rooftop, ALTITUDE Sky Lounge keeps pouring drinks with city views well past eleven.

altura.pullQuote: Save this Capitol Hill tasting menu for an anniversary or a milestone date.
altura.blurb: Big nights on Capitol Hill often end up at Altura, where a multi-course Italian tasting menu leans on Northwest ingredients. The check is firmly in special-occasion territory, so bring it out for a celebration that deserves the fuss.

ananas-pizzeria.pullQuote: Go for the weird pies, like pineapple with togarashi or the dill-heavy Lao one.
ananas-pizzeria.blurb: From the crew behind Taurus Ox, Ananas Pizzeria brings Lao flavors to pizza in First Hill. The stranger the pie, the better, and the namesake with ham, pineapple, and togarashi proves it. The Lao pie with bamboo shoots, lardon, provolone, and piles of dill is another winner, and the room handles a weeknight group dinner well.

anchorhead-coffee.pullQuote: Downtown workers, the quaffle and a spiced cold brew beat any lobby breakfast.
anchorhead-coffee.blurb: Downtown is short on morning options that aren't chain coffee or a sad pastry, which makes Anchorhead Coffee a real find. Grab a small banana bread or a biscuit sandwich, or go big with the quaffle, a cinnamon roll, croissant, and waffle hybrid. The honey bunches of cold brew, with burnt honey, cinnamon, and oat milk, is the drink to get.

andaluca-restaurant.pullQuote: A downtown Mediterranean dining room that starts serving before nine.
andaluca-restaurant.blurb: Downtown early birds can get Mediterranean food at Andaluca Restaurant, which opens in time for a breakfast meeting.

aqua-by-el-gaucho.pullQuote: Come for seafood and stay for the view over the water.
aqua-by-el-gaucho.blurb: Seafood and outdoor seating with a view pull a crowd into AQUA by El Gaucho, a polished Belltown spot.

arashi-ramen.pullQuote: A dependable Ballard bowl of ramen when the drizzle sets in.
arashi-ramen.blurb: When the weather turns gray, Arashi Ramen has steaming bowls of noodles waiting in Ballard.

archipelago.pullQuote: Book well ahead for a Filipino tasting menu that tells a personal story.
archipelago.blurb: Archipelago runs a small, story-driven tasting menu that ties Filipino-American history to Pacific Northwest ingredients. Seats are few and the bill is a splurge, so plan a real celebration around it.

armistice-coffee-roaster.pullQuote: Roosevelt locals get a careful espresso here before the workday starts.
armistice-coffee-roaster.blurb: Roosevelt's morning crowd gets coffee roasted in house at Armistice Coffee Roaster, which opens early.

aroom.pullQuote: Order the Vietnamese iced coffee topped with black sesame cream, no question.
aroom.blurb: Aroom's spare, design-studio look in Fremont hides a seriously strong Vietnamese iced coffee. Soften the jolt with a topping like salty foam, house coconut ice cream, or nutty, lightly sweet black sesame cream, which is the best of the bunch.

aroy-mak-thai-food.pullQuote: Worth crossing town for, even if three Thai places sit closer to home.
aroy-mak-thai-food.blurb: Aroy Mak Thai Food, an all-day strip mall spot up in Bitter Lake, deserves a detour from anywhere in the city. The menu stays short, with just green, yellow, and panang curries, and every one of them lands. Spice is set by the kitchen, though a chili caddy sits on the table if you want more heat, and both the chicken thigh and tofu options are excellent.

artly.pullQuote: An easy early espresso stop for anyone working downtown.
artly.blurb: Downtown commuters can count on Artly for inexpensive coffee starting first thing in the morning.

artusi.pullQuote: Grab two seats at the long bar for an easy, early-stage date.
artusi.blurb: Walking up to Artusi, you catch the smell of grilled bread and olive oil drifting from the kitchen, and the night only gets better inside. This smaller sibling to Spinasse is mostly one big L-shaped counter, and that's where you want to be for sharp cocktails and Italian snacks. It suits a newer date or any night when you want great food in lighter portions.

asadero.pullQuote: Come for wagyu sizzling on a skillet and a hibiscus margarita.
asadero.blurb: Carne asada can easily come out thin and leathery, but Asadero treats steak with real respect. Cuts like filet mignon land on a hot skillet, cooked medium rare, alongside corn tortillas, lime, and salsa for building your own tacos. There's chicken, fish, and vegetables on the menu, but the barely pink wagyu with a hibiscus margarita on the side is why you came.

assaggio-ristorante.pullQuote: A dependable Belltown Italian dining room for a relaxed weeknight dinner.
assaggio-ristorante.blurb: Anyone in Belltown looking for a sit-down Italian meal can head to Assaggio Ristorante.

atoma.pullQuote: Book the old Wallingford house when you want vegetables treated like the main event.
atoma.blurb: Plenty of pricey Seattle restaurants talk up local produce, but Atoma actually delivers on it. Expect a few familiar plates like sturgeon and beef tartare, though the vegetable cooking is where the kitchen really shines. The dining room still feels like the Wallingford home it used to be, and the check makes it a special-occasion dinner.

aviv-hummus-bar.pullQuote: Order the falafel first, then the shawarma-spiced cheeps with amba aioli.
aviv-hummus-bar.blurb: Aviv Hummus Bar up on the Hill feels like a proper sit-down lunch even though you order at the counter. Hummus is the headliner by name, but the falafel steals the plate and ranks among the city's best. Build a spread around both, and add the cheeps, shawarma-dusted fries with a garlicky amba dip.

b-z-family-mexican-restaurant.pullQuote: A family Mexican spot on Queen Anne that's already open by breakfast.
b-z-family-mexican-restaurant.blurb: Tacos and other Mexican staples are the business at B & Z Family Mexican Restaurant, with doors open early on Queen Anne.

ba-bar.pullQuote: Brisket pho and a gin cocktail in a dark, moody room is the move.
ba-bar.blurb: Ba Bar pulls off a very particular mood, bowls of brisket phở and gin drinks under low light with jazz playing. The towering bar is the first thing you see, tall enough to need a ladder and backed by a giant vintage Vietnamese rock album poster. It feels like a candlelit back alley with nice furniture, and it's open late with a happy hour worth catching.

bacco-cafe.pullQuote: An easy Market brunch stop that's open before most shops roll up their gates.
bacco-cafe.blurb: Breakfast and brunch start early at Bacco Cafe, a morning stop inside the arcade.

backyard-bagel.pullQuote: Start a Fremont morning with an inexpensive bagel before the crowds wake up.
backyard-bagel.blurb: Early Fremont mornings stay cheap and well fed thanks to Backyard Bagel.

bad-chancla.pullQuote: A Capitol Hill option when the group is craving Latin American food.
bad-chancla.blurb: On Capitol Hill, Bad Chancla is where to go for Latin American cooking.

bake-shop.pullQuote: Order the cardamom horn first then linger over a salty whipped cream latte.
bake-shop.blurb: Near the Space Needle, where good options get scarce, Bake Shop is a welcome bright spot. You can linger over natural wine or a black sesame iced latte topped with salty whipped cream, but pastries are the real reason to come. The cardamom horn eats like a gentler honey bun, and the ham and cheese pastry rolled up like a cinnamon bun beats most croissant versions.

bakery-nouveau.pullQuote: Brave the morning line for a twice-baked almond croissant you won't want to share.
bakery-nouveau.blurb: Bakery Nouveau's twice-baked almond croissant is the order, messy with toasted almond slivers and powdered sugar. It's worth braving the long morning line, claiming a table, and settling in with a hot latte. Lunch holds up too, and the croque monsieur ranks with the best ham sandwiches in town.

bangrak-market.blurb: Belltown gets a dose of Thai cooking at Bangrak Market.

bar-del-corso.pullQuote: Neapolitan pies with real char and crispness make this a Beacon Hill classic.
bar-del-corso.blurb: A big, leisurely dinner at Bar Del Corso ranks among the most reliably happy nights in Seattle. Neapolitan pizza and small plates keep this Beacon Hill Italian spot packed most evenings. The crust is charred with a light crispness all the way through, a welcome contrast to the floppier pies around town.

bar-sabine.pullQuote: Claim an alley table, order the eggplant dip, and take your time.
bar-sabine.blurb: Most Ballard patios are wedged onto the sidewalk, but Bar Sabine has an entire alley to itself, with heaters, plenty of tables, and a floral mural. Cocktails are intricate but balanced, built from things like rhubarb Aperol, sandalwood, and pistachio, sometimes with a dusting of glitter. Pair one with smoked eggplant dip, house potato chips, and other Mediterranean small plates, and know that the bar keeps going late.

bar-sur-mer.pullQuote: Take a date to this Greenwood drinks room for a late round.
bar-sur-mer.blurb: Bar Sur Mer mixes cocktails in Greenwood until well past eleven.

barnacle.pullQuote: Sip an amaro at the long wooden bar while waiting for a table next door.
barnacle.blurb: Barnacle pours beside Ballard's famous oyster bar, and it might be the cooler room. One long wood counter is the whole floor plan, a bowl of Lay's lands at your elbow, and the bartenders make drinks that embarrass a home setup. Oysters, cured meats, and cheese suit a promising date, and the early drink window is worth using.

barolo-ristorante.pullQuote: Lobster risotto and truffle-sausage gnocchi at a candlelit Westlake Italian open until 11.
barolo-ristorante.blurb: Order the lobster tail risotto with shrimp bisque, or the house gnocchi with black truffle and sausage. Dinner runs nightly from 3 to 11.

bateau.pullQuote: The old Bateau room, reopened as Jeffry's steakhouse on Union.
bateau.blurb: Bateau and Boat Bar closed, then reopened as Jeffry's in the same Capitol Hill rooms. Dry-aged steaks and steakhouse sides are the menu, and the old bar is now the front door.

baxter-frost.pullQuote: A cheap and cheerful pastry stop when you're wandering the Market.
baxter-frost.blurb: Anyone wandering Pike Place Market can grab an inexpensive pastry at Baxter & Frost.

be-mi.pullQuote: These loaded bánh mì prove that more toppings can absolutely mean better.
be-mi.blurb: Bé Mi skips the minimalist approach to bánh mì, layering on crushed peanuts, chili jam, fried shallots, and heaps of herbs. The fillings hold their own, whether it's charred, fatty pork or cold cuts with pâté. The dining room has just enough energy and makes a good escape from the Pioneer Square tour crowds.

beast-cleaver.pullQuote: Book the weekend tasting dinner for a nonstop parade of beautifully cooked meat.
beast-cleaver.blurb: By day Beast & Cleaver is a high-end Ballard butcher shop, and late in the week it turns into a tasting-menu restaurant showing off what it sells. The five-course dinner moves from beef carpaccio or rabbit rillette through clever middle courses, like a duck galantine paired with pork mousseline. Sundays bring themed meat dinners, sometimes built around a striking charcuterie board.

beecher-s-handmade-cheese.pullQuote: Brave the line of tourists for a cup of that famous mac and cheese.
beecher-s-handmade-cheese.blurb: The nutty, sharp Flagship cheddar from Beecher's Handmade Cheese is in every grocery store in town, but the Pike Place Market shop is where it all gets made. Expect a line packed with curd-sampling tourists at lunch. The reward is a creamy mac and cheese that once made Oprah's list of favorite things, and it's inexpensive.

bell-s-cookie-co.pullQuote: Walk a loop of the lake path, then reward yourself with a cookie here.
bell-s-cookie-co.blurb: Bell's Cookie Co bakes cookies near Green Lake and keeps ice cream around for a full dessert run.

ben-paris.pullQuote: Sesame-honey fried chicken and hush puppies in The State Hotel by Pike.
ben-paris.blurb: Order the buttermilk fried chicken with sesame honey and the hush puppies. Breakfast starts at 7 in this tall, brass-trimmed room steps from Pike Place.

ben-s-bread-co.pullQuote: Phinney Ridge locals line up early for loaves and pastries at this bakery.
ben-s-bread-co.blurb: Walk in early for inexpensive bread and baked goods in Phinney Ridge at Ben’s Bread Co.

betty-restaurant-bar.pullQuote: Take your parents to Queen Anne for a dressed-up New American dinner.
betty-restaurant-bar.blurb: Betty Restaurant & Bar runs a special-occasion check on Queen Anne.

biang-biang-noodles.pullQuote: Go for the wide, hand-pulled noodles and plan to get chili oil everywhere.
biang-biang-noodles.blurb: Capitol Hill noodle fans head to Biang Biang Noodles for the broad, belt-like hand-pulled noodles that give the dish its name.

big-mario-s-pizza.pullQuote: New York style slices on the Hill for when only a big fold will do.
big-mario-s-pizza.blurb: For a foldable slice on Capitol Hill, Big Mario's Pizza does the New York thing.

big-max-burger-co.pullQuote: The bacon-beef burger and herby shoestring fries are worth earning with a hike.
big-max-burger-co.blurb: Patties topped with special sauce, sharp aged cheddar, sweet onions, and thick-cut pickles are the headliners at Big Max Burger Co. The Nashville-style hot chicken sandwich, glazed with smoky chili and served with plenty of ranch, is just as good. Round things out with a milkshake, kettle corn brussels sprouts, or puffy chicken nuggets and sweet and sour sauce.

billiard-hoang.pullQuote: Get the fish sauce wings and a lemongrass vermicelli bowl, then shoot some pool.
billiard-hoang.blurb: Billiard Hoang has long been a Columbia City favorite spread by word of mouth, and it still hasn't slipped. Inside a no-frills pool hall with a roomy dining area, nearly everything on the menu is terrific and inexpensive. Those fish sauce wings are famous for good reason, and the lemongrass chicken vermicelli bowls are big enough to cover two meals.

birrieria-pepe-el-toro.pullQuote: Head here for birria tacos when you're near the University District.
birrieria-pepe-el-toro.blurb: Birrieria Pepe El Toro, as the name suggests, centers its U District menu on birria and tacos.

biscuit-bitch.pullQuote: Go hungry and order a gravy-smothered biscuit sandwich with plenty of hot sauce.
biscuit-bitch.blurb: Biscuit Bitch serves hefty breakfast biscuits stacked with fillings, and the whole menu leans into its trailer-park-to-table joke. Try The Canadian Bitch, built on banana and maple peanut butter, or the Bitchwich loaded with sausage, egg, cheese, and gravy plus hot sauce.

black-bottle.pullQuote: Swing by after work for crab dip, cauliflower, and a round of cocktails.
black-bottle.blurb: Before trading work clothes for sweatpants, stop into Black Bottle in Belltown for a drink. The menu runs long, covering Korean fried chicken bites, spicy cauliflower, and a cheesy Dungeness crab dip, so you can mix it up on every visit. There's a happy hour.

bluwater-bistro-leschi.pullQuote: Grab an outdoor table on a sunny day and watch the lake.
bluwater-bistro-leschi.blurb: Lake Washington views from the outdoor seating are the main draw at BluWater Bistro - Leschi.

bongos-cafe.pullQuote: After a Green Lake loop, bring the dog and order jerk chicken.
bongos-cafe.blurb: Bongos Cafe lives in a brightly painted old gas station by the lake, and the beachy patio always feels like a party. The jerk chicken is excellent, the Caribbean sandwiches stand up to the best around, and the fried yucca balls come filled with molten cheese. Wash it all down with a coconut-heavy piña, and brace yourself for the spicy shrimp.

bonito-cafe-y-mercadito.pullQuote: An early Capitol Hill coffee stop with a little Mexican market attached.
bonito-cafe-y-mercadito.blurb: Bonito Cafe Y Mercadito pours coffee and sells Mexican goods on Capitol Hill, opening early and staying gentle on a weekday budget.

bottega-gabriele.pullQuote: Great constantly changing menu, I went for the Hot Honey Piccante.
bottega-gabriele.blurb: Great constantly changing menu, I went for the Hot Honey Piccante.

bottega-italiana.pullQuote: Grab a cup of gelato here while you wander the Market.
bottega-italiana.blurb: Italian-style ice cream justifies stopping at stop at Bottega Italiana inside the arcade.

bottlehouse.pullQuote: A neighborhood wine bar in Madrona for a relaxed glass after work.
bottlehouse.blurb: Madrona has its own easygoing wine stop in Bottlehouse.

bounty-kitchen.pullQuote: Gluten-free diners should head straight for the pancakes with cinnamon butter.
bounty-kitchen.blurb: If gluten is your nemesis, Bounty Kitchen belongs on your brunch shortlist. The bright all-day cafe on Queen Anne makes excellent gluten-free pancakes topped with fruit compote and cinnamon butter, plus egg and vegetable hashes. Wheat-friendly tables can go for the braised beef bowl or avocado toast, and expect a short wait during the weekend rush.

buckley-s.pullQuote: Rally a big group here to watch the game and eat bar food.
buckley-s.blurb: Game days in Belltown mean a crowd at Buckley's, a sports bar with plenty of room for groups and a kitchen open late.

cactus.pullQuote: Butternut squash enchiladas and margaritas at the corner of Terry and Harrison.
cactus.blurb: Order the butternut squash enchiladas with apricot-chocolate mole rojo, or the brisket tacos on fresh corn tortillas. Weekend brunch runs 10 to 2.

cafe-campagne.pullQuote: Come for weekend brunch, when the room is loud and the bread is crusty.
cafe-campagne.blurb: Café Campagne has been cooking French comfort food in Post Alley for more than forty years, and the dining room still channels a Paris bistro with old posters and lamps made from wine bottles. Dinner is mellow and the steak frites are great, but brunch is when this place comes alive. Market crowds spill in to share fluffy egg dishes and good bread over upbeat music, and the check lands in special-occasion range.

cafe-flora.pullQuote: Bring your meat-loving friends and don't mention that everything here is vegetarian.
cafe-flora.blurb: Take your carnivore friends to Cafe Flora and maybe skip the part where you mention it's meat-free. Smoked mozzarella pizza and mushroom risotto make a real argument for meatless cooking, and the airy greenhouse feel of the room helps too. The door opens before nine, so brunch is fair game.

cafe-hagen.pullQuote: Settle onto the astroturf patio with a lavender oat milk latte.
cafe-hagen.blurb: Built around the Danish idea of hygge, Café Hagen is a cozy escape amid South Lake Union's tech offices. There's an astroturf patio, lavender oat lattes, and enough houseplants to make the whole place feel calm, and the door opens before nine.

cafe-lolo.pullQuote: Share a couple of salads and order the soft wheat porridge at lunch.
cafe-lolo.blurb: Counter service, folk murals, and fizzy pop music give Cafe Lolo on Capitol Hill a soothing, unhurried feel. The menu goes well past standard soups and sandwiches, with seasonal twists like melon topped with coppa and plum agrodolce, plus pasta made from house-milled flour. At lunch, split a few salads and a bowl of soft wheat porridge, and leave room for the blintzes.

cafe-turko.pullQuote: Book a summer patio lunch here for mezze and kebabs.
cafe-turko.blurb: Mezze and kebabs at Café Turko in Fremont are good enough that you'll stop worrying about the metal tea kettle dangling overhead. The room suits a summer lunch on the patio, a casual date, or weeknight takeout.

caffe-umbria.pullQuote: Stop in for an Italian-style espresso before the workday kicks off.
caffe-umbria.blurb: Early risers by the south end of the lake can count on Caffè Umbria for a proper coffee.

caffe-vita.pullQuote: A reliable neighborhood espresso stop before a show at Seattle Center.
caffe-vita.blurb: Lower Queen Anne's early risers get house-roasted coffee at Caffe Vita, and it won't cost much.

calozzi-s-cheesesteaks-georgetown.pullQuote: Always add fried onions, and go for the whiz if your shirt can handle it.
calozzi-s-cheesesteaks-georgetown.blurb: Easy to miss and easy to trip into, Calozzi's Cheesesteaks Georgetown is a tiny roadside shack that handles any Philly craving. The beef is shaved paper thin and piled so high you'll lose some before it reaches your mouth, and while it can run a little dry, the flavor is excellent. It's an inexpensive lunch, too.

canlis.pullQuote: Dress up and celebrate here, where the lake view does half the work.
canlis.blurb: Since the fifties, Canlis has been the city's go-to for big celebrations, set in a mid-century modern house perched above Lake Union. Service is famously polished, the tall windows put the water front and center, and the check matches the occasion. Book it for an anniversary, a proposal, or a parents' visit.

canon.pullQuote: Settle in with the encyclopedic menu and order something served in a light bulb.
canon.blurb: Canon on Capitol Hill treats cocktails like a fantasy factory, with a menu that runs for pages of classics and inventive originals. Drinks might involve smoke, rinses, house syrups, or a scoop of Cap'n Crunch ice cream, and they arrive in vessels like nesting dolls, glass hearts, or IV bags. The back bar is a towering wall of bottles, and the place now takes walk-ins only, with the bar going late.

cantinetta.pullQuote: Bring a date to Wallingford for an Italian dinner that feels relaxed.
cantinetta.blurb: Couples looking for an Italian date night in Wallingford can count on Cantinetta.

capitale-pizzeria.blurb: For pizza on Capitol Hill, Capitale Pizzeria lands on the neighborhood's shortlist of reliable pies.

cardoon.pullQuote: Get the licorice caramel latte and dunk a cardamom rose cookie in it.
cardoon.blurb: This tiny Ballard cafe pulls Kuma espresso with Chinese and German touches, and its oat lattes come out impossibly silky. A salty licorice caramel drink brings a gentle anise edge. Sunlight pours through the windows at Cardoon, the snug corner seats are surprisingly comfortable, and the doors open early.

carmelo-s-tacos.pullQuote: Thick handmade tortillas and that chorizo, potato, and cactus filling are the move.
carmelo-s-tacos.blurb: Carmelo's Tacos presses its own hefty tortillas and fills them with well-marinated carne asada or a chorizo, potato, and nopal mix that sticks with you. Burrito people should know the cheese gets a quick sear on the griddle before it goes in. It's cheap, it's fast, and the Capitol Hill counter keeps going late.

carmine-s.pullQuote: Rigatoni Bolognese under the soaring rotunda windows downtown.
carmine-s.blurb: Order the rigatoni Bolognese, a Carmine family classic, or the newer osso buco ravioli. It's the Smeraldo family's downtown room, after Il Terrazzo.

charlotte-restaurant-lounge.pullQuote: Book it for the skyline views and a dinner that feels like an occasion.
charlotte-restaurant-lounge.blurb: High up in the Lotte Hotel, Charlotte Restaurant & Lounge pairs New American plates with sweeping views over downtown and the water. The bill belongs to a celebration, so save it for anniversaries and visiting parents who love a view.

cheba-hut-toasted-subs.pullQuote: Cheap toasted subs that hit hardest when it's late and you're starving.
cheba-hut-toasted-subs.blurb: A stoner-themed chain counter near the university, Cheba Hut Toasted Subs keeps the oven running late and the prices low.

cheese-room-seattle.pullQuote: A cheap Capitol Hill sandwich counter that's easy to slot into lunch.
cheese-room-seattle.blurb: Inexpensive sandwiches are the whole business at Cheese Room Seattle, a Capitol Hill counter.

chengdu-taste.pullQuote: Bring friends with a high spice tolerance and order more than you need.
chengdu-taste.blurb: Chengdu Taste brings fiery Sichuan cooking to the Chinatown-International District.

chez-phinney.pullQuote: Self-pour wine machines and late-night dance music make this the north end's best wine stop.
chez-phinney.blurb: Hand over a card, grab an empty glass, and work your way through the self-serve taps at Chez Phinney. Snack on house chocolate truffles plus Michou Deli dips between pours. By day the room looks like a Parisian cafe inside an airport terminal, but after dark the music gets loud and nobody's rushing you out.

chuck-s-hop-shop.pullQuote: Wall-to-wall coolers, a deep tap list, and a crowd that treats it like a living room.
chuck-s-hop-shop.blurb: Chuck's Hop Shop pairs a long run of taps with coolers packed with bottles and cans. You can linger past eleven.

chung-chun-rice-dog.pullQuote: Get a mozzarella dog, add sugar and ketchup, and don't overthink it.
chung-chun-rice-dog.blurb: Korean-style corn dogs in a crisp rice-flour batter are the specialty at Chung Chun Rice Dog, including cheesy and potato-studded versions. It's an inexpensive snack stop in the Chinatown-International District.

cinnamon-works.pullQuote: Grab a cinnamon roll early, before the Market crowds take over.
cinnamon-works.blurb: Among the market stalls, Cinnamon Works sells big, inexpensive pastries starting first thing in the morning.

cinque-terre-ristorante.pullQuote: Skip the pricey entrees and order the margherita with a pasta on the side.
cinque-terre-ristorante.blurb: Blue neon under the bar and champagne bottles as decor make Cinque Terre Ristorante feel a bit like a hotel lobby. Ignore that, because the Neapolitan pies are the real deal, with a charred, crackly crust and a balanced layer of San Marzano and mozzarella. Round things out with casarecce tossed with pesto and ricotta, or boar sugo over rigatoni, and leave the main courses alone.

citizen-collective.pullQuote: An inexpensive Lower Queen Anne coffee stop that keeps going long after dark.
citizen-collective.blurb: Citizen Collective pours coffee by Seattle Center from early morning until late at night.

ciudad-grill.pullQuote: A dependable pick for grilled meat and flatbread with almost any crowd.
ciudad-grill.blurb: Not every dinner needs to change your life, and Ciudad Grill knows it. This Georgetown spot is reliably easygoing, with a charcoal grill you notice before you even walk in. Expect smoky charred meats and warm flatbreads that suit a date, coworkers, or your in-laws equally well.

cobb-s-pike-place-popcorn.pullQuote: An easy, cheap snack stop for grazing your way through the Market.
cobb-s-pike-place-popcorn.blurb: Snack on cheap popcorn from Cobb's Pike Place Popcorn while you wander the Market.

coffeeholic-house.pullQuote: Come early for a strong, sweet coffee and a seat to settle in.
coffeeholic-house.blurb: Coffeeholic House pours Vietnamese-leaning coffee drinks in Columbia City, and the doors open early.

communion-restaurant-bar.pullQuote: Order the stewed pork neck and save serious room for peach cobbler.
communion-restaurant-bar.blurb: Communion Restaurant & Bar sits in the Liberty Bank Building and cooks like a tribute to both the American South and the Central District around it. Berbere-rubbed chicken over lemony lentils tips its hat to the neighborhood's Ethiopian community, while the pork neck is pure Southern comfort. The bill belongs to a celebration, and the meal earns it.

cookie-s-country-chicken.pullQuote: Fried chicken from a counter, which is exactly how lunch should go.
cookie-s-country-chicken.blurb: A no-fuss Pioneer Square counter, Cookie’s Country Chicken is all about the fried bird.

copper-tree-coffee-house.pullQuote: An early-opening Capitol Hill coffee shop for the commute or a slow morning.
copper-tree-coffee-house.blurb: Copper Tree Coffee House opens early for Capitol Hill coffee runs, and the prices stay low.

cornelly.pullQuote: Book it for date night when everyone at the table is craving Italian.
cornelly.blurb: Cornelly makes a strong case for an Italian dinner date on Capitol Hill.

cortina.pullQuote: Bucatini and bone-marrow meatballs at Two Union Square.
cortina.blurb: Get the bucatini with beef-and-ricotta meatballs in a marrow-enriched tomato sauce. The pasta is made fresh daily, and the pizza dough proofs for three days.

cotto-belltown.pullQuote: Late Italian in Belltown for when a bar menu just won't do.
cotto-belltown.blurb: Cotto Belltown serves Italian food and keeps the kitchen going late, which counts for a lot around here.

creamy-cone-cafe.pullQuote: Stack lemon raspberry cheesecake and banana pudding in one waffle cone.
creamy-cone-cafe.blurb: Two scoops define Creamy Cone Cafe in Rainier Beach. The cheesecake flavor is bright and tart, with raspberry ribbons and graham crumbles, and the banana pudding eats like a frozen smoothie loaded with wafer cookies. The folks behind the counter are genuinely warm, and morning service starts first.

d-la-santa.pullQuote: Easy to drive past for years, and a pleasant shock once you finally stop.
d-la-santa.blurb: D' La Santa hides in plain sight on a quiet stretch of north Capitol Hill, and plenty of locals have passed it without noticing. Finding it feels like discovering cash in an old coat pocket. Grab street parking and settle in for a Mexican meal that rewards the detour.

dahlia-bakery.pullQuote: Get the breakfast sandwich and a few coconut cream pie bites to go.
dahlia-bakery.blurb: Dahlia Bakery's pastry case runs deep, but the move is a breakfast sandwich stacked with egg, ham, pepper jack, arugula, and spicy jalapeño aioli. The house English muffins taste nothing like the supermarket kind, which turns out to be a good thing. Seating amounts to a few spots outside, so plan on eating on the go in Belltown.

damn-the-weather.pullQuote: Order the fennel-dusted fries cooked in chicken fat, then a cocktail, then the burger.
damn-the-weather.blurb: A brick-walled hideout from the drizzle, Damn the Weather cooks far better than a bar needs to. Cocktails come first, but the kitchen sends out parm-heavy spaghetti bolognese, bright crudo, and blistered shishitos. It's usually packed and open late, so be ready to circle for a seat.

daniel-s-broiler.pullQuote: A classic steakhouse splurge with lake views that make the bill easier to swallow.
daniel-s-broiler.blurb: Right on the water at Lake Union, Daniel's Broiler does old-school steak dinners with big cuts and bigger views. Expect a milestone bill, and plan it around sunset if you can.

dantini.pullQuote: A low-key Interbay pizza option that deserves more attention than it gets.
dantini.blurb: Dantini turns out pizza in Interbay and keeps getting mentioned among the city's better pies.

darkalino-s.pullQuote: Grab a bar seat solo and twirl through a plate of amatriciana.
darkalino-s.blurb: Darkalino's took over the old London Plane space in Pioneer Square, keeping the towering columns, huge windows, and all that brick. The all-day Italian menu is casual, and the pasta all'amatriciana is the thing to get. Romance isn't really the vibe, so come alone or bring a crew of friends while wedding-reception hits play overhead.

dave-s-hot-chicken.pullQuote: Pick a heat level one notch below your ego and order the sliders.
dave-s-hot-chicken.blurb: Nashville-style hot chicken tenders and sliders make up nearly the whole menu at Dave's Hot Chicken, with spice that runs from mild to genuinely painful. The Capitol Hill counter keeps it cheap.

dead-line.pullQuote: Come at happy hour, when the chips, olives, and nuts arrive free with drinks.
dead-line.blurb: Dead Line is small, dark, and polished, with shelves of bottles so tall the bartenders need a rolling ladder. Beyond the serious cocktails, the kitchen turns out South American small plates like brisket arepas and squash al pastor tacos. The pre-dinner window is a steal, and the bar pours past eleven.

deep-dive.pullQuote: Worth the long wait for a celebratory round under the sea.
deep-dive.blurb: Deep Dive comes from the team behind The Walrus and the Carpenter, and it feels like a fancy aquarium dreamed up by Disney. Getting in is a project, since the entrance tucks into the Amazon Spheres and reservations aren't a thing. Expect to wait an hour or more, then order something festive and toast whatever you came to celebrate.

deep-sea-sugar-salt.pullQuote: The Funfetti slice, with cream cheese frosting and a hint of almond, wins.
deep-sea-sugar-salt.blurb: Deep Sea Sugar & Salt bakes gorgeous layer cakes in Georgetown, with flavors like dark chocolate spiked with local porter or earl grey with bergamot mascarpone. Whole cakes aren't cheap, but slices make an easy treat. People line up before opening, though you can also reserve same-day slices online in the morning.

delancey.pullQuote: Ballard's candlelit wood-fired pies prove Seattle belongs in the great pizza conversation.
delancey.blurb: Seattle can hold its own as a pizza town, and Delancey is the proof. Start with burrata swimming in pesto or the towering Jersey Salad, then focus on the blistered pies topped with fennel sausage, sweet Walla Walla onions, or kalamatas. The dim room smells like the oven and works for date night or dinner with the family.

delaurenti.pullQuote: Build a picnic from the cheese counter, then grab a cannoli filled on the spot.
delaurenti.blurb: DeLaurenti stocks shelves of imported and local pantry goods among the market stalls, from olive oils and jams to a dangerously good bag of black truffle chips. Upstairs you'll find a smart wine and beer selection, and the charcuterie and cheese case is excellent. Grab a cold cut sandwich up front, and don't skip the chocolate chip cookie or Linzer tarts.

di-fiora.blurb: Di Fiora cooks Asian fusion dishes for the First Hill neighborhood.

dick-s-drive-in.pullQuote: A Deluxe, fries, and a chocolate shake is a Seattle rite of passage.
dick-s-drive-in.blurb: Dick's Drive-In has been slinging cheap burgers, fresh-cut fries, and thick milkshakes since the middle of the last century. Walk up, order fast, and eat in the car like generations of locals before you.

din-tai-fung.pullQuote: Order the pork soup dumplings by the dozen and don't skip the green beans.
din-tai-fung.blurb: Dumpling makers work behind glass at Din Tai Fung near the university, pleating pork xiao long bao with famously tidy folds. Fill out the table with garlicky green beans and cucumber salad, and expect a wait at peak hours.

dingfelder-s-delicatessen.pullQuote: Get the pastrami on rye and a pickle, and you're set until dinner.
dingfelder-s-delicatessen.blurb: East Coast Jewish deli energy comes to Capitol Hill at Dingfelder's Delicatessen, where piled-high pastrami sandwiches carry the meal. Morning service starts first and keeps the prices friendly.

dino-s-tomato-pie.pullQuote: Claim the big round booth in back and order garlic knots for the table.
dino-s-tomato-pie.blurb: Dino's Tomato Pie shares owners with Delancey but goes the opposite direction, trading minimalism for dim, old-school pizzeria charm. The charred pies are the draw, and the vodka sauce version is a crowd favorite. Bring your whole crew and try to grab the chandelier booth.

doce-donut-co.pullQuote: An early-morning donut stop in Wallingford that's easy on the wallet.
doce-donut-co.blurb: Wallingford's early risers get their inexpensive sugar fix at DOCE Donut Co.

dog-in-the-park.pullQuote: A cheap downtown hot dog when lunch needs to happen in five minutes.
dog-in-the-park.blurb: Dog in the Park handles quick, inexpensive franks for Downtown lunch breaks.

donna-s.blurb: Donna's pours drinks on the Hill and makes the cut among the neighborhood's better bars.

dough-zone.pullQuote: Come hungry for soup dumplings and let everything else play backup.
dough-zone.blurb: Dough Zone moves fast, and the soup dumplings are the reason to come, thin-skinned and full of hot broth. Round out the order with whatever noodles or buns catch your eye in this Chinatown-International District dining room.

dreamland.pullQuote: Order a disco ball of margaritas and the gooey cheeseburger, then claim the balcony.
dreamland.blurb: Dreamland looks like a space jungle grotto stitched together from sci-fi movies and roller disco fantasy, and it's a blast. Head for the patio for drag brunch or a night with friends, and grab grasshopper slushies or Jell-O shots for the table. The bar snacks are excellent, especially that burger, and the party runs late.

driftwood.pullQuote: Stick with spritzes, small plates, and the excellent bread, and you'll leave happy.
driftwood.blurb: Pastel, polished, and very Alki, Driftwood calls for dressing up a little while keeping the sandals on. The seafood mains can get fussy with too many toppings, but the cocktails are refreshing and the smaller dishes hold up nicely. Order the table bread, which ranks with the city's best, and make it a date.

due-cucina-italiana.pullQuote: A Capitol Hill Italian option for an easygoing weeknight bowl of something comforting.
due-cucina-italiana.blurb: Due' Cucina Italiana cooks Italian food on Capitol Hill for neighborhood dinners.

duke-s-seafood-south-lake-union.pullQuote: Grab a deck table at happy hour and order a cup of chowder.
duke-s-seafood-south-lake-union.blurb: Lake Union views and a packed deck pull a crowd into Duke's Seafood South Lake Union, along with the creamy clam chowder the local chain built its name on. The pre-dinner window is a solid deal.

earl-s-on-the-ave.pullQuote: Show up as a crowd, find a screen, and keep the tab cheap.
earl-s-on-the-ave.blurb: Cheap drinks, games on the TVs, and room for a big group make Earl's on the Ave a U District standby that stays open late.

eggslut.pullQuote: The Fairfax on a warm brioche bun fixes almost any rough morning.
eggslut.blurb: The LA egg sandwich chain Eggslut landed on Capitol Hill, and the Fairfax, with soft scrambled eggs, chives, cheddar, and sriracha mayo on a brioche bun, is the order regulars make. Doors open early, and the bill stays gentle enough for a weekday treat.

el-gaucho.pullQuote: Dress up, order a dry-aged steak, and let the tableside show unfold.
el-gaucho.blurb: Dim lights, live piano, and servers working tableside carts make El Gaucho the old-school supper club Belltown never outgrew. Get a dry-aged cut with a Caesar tossed right in front of you. Bring a fat budget, since this is a special-occasion check through and through.

eldr.pullQuote: A Ballard dinner pick for New American plates once the craving is special.
eldr.blurb: For contemporary American plates in Ballard, book a table at ELDR.

elysian-brewing-capitol-hill.pullQuote: Gather a big group, order pints of Space Dust, and settle in.
elysian-brewing-capitol-hill.blurb: Big tables, a long tap list, and Space Dust IPA at the source make Elysian Brewing - Capitol Hill a simple yes for groups. Happy hour helps, and the pub keeps pouring late.

empire-roasters-and-records.pullQuote: Pair a made-to-order Belgian waffle with the house cashew milk latte.
empire-roasters-and-records.blurb: Empire Roasters and Records fits into a slim converted garage in Columbia City, and the food punches way above coffee-shop standards. Waffles are made fresh when you order, crowned with blueberries and a snowfall of sugar, or kept simple with butter and maple. Gluten-free and vegan versions are available, and the date-sweetened cashew drink deserves a spot on your tray.

espresso-vivace.pullQuote: Order a ristretto and sip it slowly, because this is Seattle's espresso benchmark.
espresso-vivace.blurb: Espresso Vivace pulls the best shots in town, and the obsessive care shows in every cup. The room hums steadily without getting so packed you can't work, and on warm days a roll-up door opens the whole cafe to the sidewalk. Drop your drink on the way out and they'll make you another, no charge.

family-donut.pullQuote: Get the buttermilk bar and a fruit-glazed donut, and arrive early on weekends.
family-donut.blurb: Family Donut in Northgate makes the city's best donuts for very little money. Glazes get their flavor from real blueberries, orange zest, and raspberry, while old fashioneds stay tender inside under crunchy ridges. You'll even get a free donut hole on a stick as you leave, but show up early on Saturday and Sunday before the cases empty.

familyfriend.pullQuote: Bring a date to Beacon Hill for Chamorro and Filipino flavors done with care.
familyfriend.blurb: Familyfriend cooks Chamorro and Filipino food on Beacon Hill, and it makes a strong date-night pick.

farestart-restaurant.pullQuote: Eat well and help fund culinary job training while you're at it.
farestart-restaurant.blurb: Every meal at FareStart Restaurant supports a nonprofit program, with students learning the ropes in the kitchen and on the floor. The American menu is approachable, and it opens early enough for a Denny Triangle breakfast meeting.

fat-s-chicken-waffles.pullQuote: Order the chicken and waffles with Hennessy butter and a spiked fruit punch.
fat-s-chicken-waffles.blurb: Fat's Chicken & Waffles is where you go when the laundry can wait but the craving can't. The waffles are thin and airy with a pat of cognac butter, and the fried chicken holds its crunch even after the drive home. Eat in the laid-back Central District dining room, sweatpants welcome, with a sweet tea or boozy punch.

firn.pullQuote: Head onto the roof deck for cocktails that stretch well past eleven.
firn.blurb: Firn mixes drinks high above Pioneer Square and keeps going late.

fob-poke-bar.pullQuote: Build-your-own poke bowls with house FOB sauce on Blanchard Street.
fob-poke-bar.blurb: Build a salmon or tuna bowl over rice or greens, and finish it with the house FOB sauce, a Hawaiian shoyu blend, and the zesty mango.

fob-sushi-bar.pullQuote: Belltown sushi that can stand alone on a crowded list of contenders.
fob-sushi-bar.blurb: FOB Sushi Bar handles raw fish in Belltown and earns a mention among the city's better sushi spots.

fog-room.pullQuote: Take visitors up for a cocktail with the city spread out below.
fog-room.blurb: Fog Room pours drinks on a Downtown rooftop with skyline views, and you can linger past eleven.

fogon-cocina-mexicana.pullQuote: Don't leave without the al pastor tacos, and add the boozy fajitas.
fogon-cocina-mexicana.blurb: Fogón Cocina Mexicana is loud in the best way, with lime-green walls and cooks pressing fresh tortillas up front. The fajitas get a splash of tequila, beer, and wine, and they're excellent, but al pastor tacos are the real must. It can hold a crowd dinner or a solo seat at the bar.

footprint-wine-tap.pullQuote: A low-key weeknight hang for anyone who actually likes talking about grapes.
footprint-wine-tap.blurb: The taps behind the bar at Footprint Wine Tap give away its past life as a growler fill station, but now every line pours wine. It's a mellow Capitol Hill stop for people who genuinely care about viticulture. There's even a trivia game to test your vineyard knowledge.

fortuna-bottega.pullQuote: Cheap Italian sandwiches in Greenwood, no reservation needed, just show up hungry.
fortuna-bottega.blurb: Fortuna Bottega makes inexpensive Italian sandwiches at a walk-up Greenwood counter.

founders-club.pullQuote: A downtown drinks room for a nightcap that turns into a second round.
founders-club.blurb: Founders Club mixes polished drinks in the Downtown core and keeps the bar open late.

fram.pullQuote: Order a honey lavender latte, claim the window seat, and pretend to work.
fram.blurb: Fram squeezes a lot of fun into a room about the size of a single garage. Lavender lattes sweetened with honey and constantly churning frosé lead the menu, and the fridge holds a good stash of cans and bottles. Strong wifi makes it a natural work spot, though the nearby lake makes a coffee walk awfully tempting.

frankie-jo-s.pullQuote: Dairy-free scoops so good you'll forget anything was missing in the first place.
frankie-jo-s.blurb: Frankie & Jo's makes Seattle's best ice cream without a drop of dairy or a speck of wheat. The cultured crème fraîche flavor, swirled with berries and studded with lemon cake, is unforgettable, and oat milk vanilla loaded with brown sugar blondies is close behind. Get your scoops in a house maple oat waffle cone, and know the Hill shop stays open late.

fremont-brewing.pullQuote: Bring takeout barbecue and spend a long afternoon at the picnic tables.
fremont-brewing.blurb: Fremont Brewing is daytime drinking at its most generous, with a sprawling patio, long communal tables, and free pretzels. Two infused Randall taps rotate constantly, so there's always something new to try. Outside food is welcome, which means a sack of Roro BBQ and a flight make a great Fremont outing.

fuji-bakery.pullQuote: Get the curry bread warm and a few pastries for later.
fuji-bakery.blurb: Fuji Bakery brings Japanese bakery sensibilities to Queen Anne, with flaky French-style pastries alongside savory buns. The crunchy curry bread is a must, and prices stay low enough to grab extras before the street is busy.

g-h-pasta-pizza.pullQuote: A West Seattle neighborhood pick when the family can't agree between pizza and pasta.
g-h-pasta-pizza.blurb: Locals lean on G.H. Pasta & Pizza for West Seattle pizza and pasta nights.

gelatiamo.pullQuote: Order the rice gelato, which tastes like rice pudding straight from the freezer.
gelatiamo.blurb: Gelatiamo scoops the city's best gelato and gets you as close to a Roman vacation as Downtown Seattle allows. Every flavor is solid, stracciatella included, but the rice flavor is the one people talk about. It's creamy, gently sweet, and refreshingly free of cinnamon.

general-porpoise.pullQuote: Vanilla custard doughnuts under Jeffry Mitchell's elephant lanterns in Pioneer Square.
general-porpoise.blurb: Get the vanilla custard doughnut, then a lemon tiramisu if it's in the case. It closes at 3, so come in the morning.

georgetown-brewing.pullQuote: Drink a pint of Manny's where it's brewed, ideally with a friend you've neglected.
georgetown-brewing.blurb: Georgetown Brewing makes Manny's, the pale ale that seems to be on every tap in Seattle. The gravel-lot tasting room is where to try it fresh alongside other pales, IPAs, and a chocolatey porter. Bring a big group or an old friend you owe a catch-up.

geraldine-s-counter.pullQuote: Go on a weekday morning and claim a swivel stool at the counter.
geraldine-s-counter.blurb: Every neighborhood deserves a diner as cheerful as Geraldine's Counter, where the coffee refills never stop coming. Take a window seat, soak up the Rainier Avenue light, and work through crisp french toast and thick-cut bacon. Weekend waits run long, so a quieter weekday is the smarter play.

ghost-alley-espresso.pullQuote: Skip the gum wall selfies and get a nutella latte instead.
ghost-alley-espresso.blurb: Tucked beside the gum wall, Ghost Alley Espresso is a tiny walk-up window that rescues any Pike Place errand. The lattes run playful, with nutella and blueberry cheesecake among the options, and the house nut milks are a real draw. It's inexpensive, quick, and far better than lingering with the tourists outside.

ghost-note-coffee.pullQuote: Order the espresso float and discover that root beer belongs in coffee.
ghost-note-coffee.blurb: The baristas at Ghost Note Coffee reach for cocktail shakers as often as steam wands. That precision shows in a smoked grapefruit and rosemary cold espresso served in a coupe, and in a malty mocha shake brightened with orange peel. The real showstopper is the espresso float, which pairs iced latte with local root beer and vegan cream.

glo-s.pullQuote: Brave the weekend line, because these hash browns justify every minute of it.
glo-s.blurb: Glo’s moved off its old Olive Way corner but kept the neon, the stone walls, and the mid-century charm. The wait still stretches past an hour on weekends, and it still pays off. Expect hash browns with a shattering golden crust, scallion and garlic scrambles, and a tangy homemade corned beef hash.

goldfinch-tavern.pullQuote: Request glass-side seating at sunset and let the Elliott Bay view do the work.
goldfinch-tavern.blurb: Inside the Four Seasons downtown, Goldfinch Tavern serves polished American food with big windows facing the water. It opens early for breakfast and keeps the bar going late, so the room suits a morning meeting or a nightcap.

grand-central-bakery.pullQuote: Grab a rustic loaf and a pastry for the walk home.
grand-central-bakery.blurb: For decades, Grand Central Bakery has been a Seattle name for crusty, rustic bread. The Wallingford shop opens early, so stop in for a morning croissant and leave with a loaf under your arm.

grappa.pullQuote: Bring your parents here for a polished Mediterranean dinner on Queen Anne.
grappa.blurb: On Queen Anne, Grappa serves Mediterranean food that suits date night or a dinner with the folks.

grillbird.pullQuote: This is the West Seattle stop for rotisserie chicken that skips the gluten.
grillbird.blurb: The rotisserie chicken at Grillbird in West Seattle comes from a gluten-free kitchen.

hamdi.pullQuote: Skip the dry-aged steak and build your meal from the mezze instead.
hamdi.blurb: Hamdi grew from a brewery pop-up into a special-occasion Turkish restaurant built around a big open wood-fired grill. The servers will push the steaks, but the smarter move is a spread of small plates, like a garlicky celery root dip studded with dried figs. A watermelon salad with warm spices and salty Tulum cheese is another reason to order light and still enjoy the show.

harry-s-beach-house.pullQuote: Grab a rooftop seat on a clear day and order the seafood.
harry-s-beach-house.blurb: Harry's Beach House brings seafood, an open-air roof deck, and morning hours to West Seattle.

harry-s-fine-foods.pullQuote: An early Capitol Hill breakfast here makes an easy win with visiting parents.
harry-s-fine-foods.blurb: Opening early for breakfast and brunch, Harry’s Fine Foods serves New American cooking that suits a meal with the folks.

harvest-beat.pullQuote: Book the single nightly seating for a vegan tasting menu worth celebrating.
harvest-beat.blurb: Harvest Beat makes the case that a special occasion doesn't need meat or butter. There's one seating each night, kicked off by a gong and a speech from the chef about the farmers and foragers behind dishes like carrot ginger bisque and a cashew paneer loaf. Wine pairing is part of the deal, though the fresh-pressed elixir pairing is the more interesting route, and a berry bread pudding often closes things out with birthday candles.

hellenika-cultured-creamery.pullQuote: Cool off between Pike Place errands with a cup of tangy frozen yogurt.
hellenika-cultured-creamery.blurb: Frozen yogurt and gelato come cheap at HELLENIKA Cultured Creamery inside the arcade.

hello-robin.pullQuote: Get the cookie ice cream sandwich with Molly Moon's and an espresso.
hello-robin.blurb: Fresh cookies are the whole point at Hello Robin, a Capitol Hill shop baking everything from classic chocolate chip to a blueberry pancake version. Buy them baked, take home dough, or have two pressed around a scoop of Molly Moon's. An espresso bar makes it an easy afternoon treat.

hey-bagel.pullQuote: Hot, never-toasted bagels to rip and dip in schmear.
hey-bagel.blurb: Get the everything bagel hot and tear it into a tub of spicy scallion schmear. No slicing, no sandwiches. Named best bagel at BagelFest West 2026.

hi-spot-cafe.pullQuote: Order the breakfast burrito and plan to skip lunch entirely.
hi-spot-cafe.blurb: Set in a converted Madrona house, Hi Spot Cafe still feels warm and homey, with tables spread across the upstairs rooms. The pancakes and scrambles are solid, but the hulking breakfast burrito with black beans, eggs, and vegetables is the order. It arrives with potatoes, tomatillo salsa, and sour cream you should spread over every bite.

homer.pullQuote: Fill the table with dips and warm pita, then save room for soft serve.
homer.blurb: Homer brings Mediterranean cooking to Beacon Hill with a wood-fired oven at the center of the room. Puffy pita and spreads anchor the meal, and the soft serve is a sweet way to end it.

honeyhole-sandwiches.pullQuote: Late-night sandwich cravings on Capitol Hill have a reliable answer right here.
honeyhole-sandwiches.blurb: Cheap sandwiches and a kitchen that runs late make Honeyhole Sandwiches a Capitol Hill standby.

hood-famous.pullQuote: Order an ube latte and a slice of ube cheesecake to go.
hood-famous.blurb: Hood Famous built its name on Filipino baked goods, and its Chinatown-International District cafe pairs them with early coffee service. Ube shows up everywhere, from the lattes to the cheesecake that made the bakery a local favorite.

hot-cakes.pullQuote: Get the molten cake, but don't overlook the soft serve with magic shell.
hot-cakes.blurb: Molten chocolate cakes are the specialty at Hot Cakes, with peanut butter and s'mores versions, plus a vegan version. The sleeper hit is vanilla soft serve under a shell of smoked chocolate. The Capitol Hill shop stays open late, which makes dessert after dinner easy.

house-of-eve.pullQuote: Start a Belltown night with a cocktail here before heading to dinner.
house-of-eve.blurb: Cocktails lead the menu at House Of Eve, a bar in Belltown.

how-to-cook-a-wolf.pullQuote: Settle into the snug room and order a couple of handmade pastas.
how-to-cook-a-wolf.blurb: Named after a wartime cookbook, How to Cook a Wolf turns out fresh pasta and Italian small plates in an intimate Queen Anne room. The kitchen runs late, so Queen Anne can still get pasta after the first plan falls through.

hushy-s-sandwiches.pullQuote: Come in with friends or solo, best turkey sandwich around.
hushy-s-sandwiches.blurb: Come in with friends or solo, best turkey sandwich around.

il-bistro.pullQuote: Cioppino in a candlelit grotto under Pike Place.
il-bistro.blurb: Order the cioppino or the rigatoni Bolognese in this candlelit room down a cobblestone alley under the market, open for more than 50 years.

il-nido.pullQuote: This is where West Seattle goes for anniversaries and unfussy pasta nights alike.
il-nido.blurb: Alki may feel like a summer-only scene, but il nido gives West Seattle a reason to go out all year. The Italian cooking is consistent enough that even a plain bowl of noodles lands, and the staff handles off-menu requests without blinking. It sits inside a historic homestead, which makes the setting feel special without getting stuffy.

il-terrazzo-carmine.pullQuote: Marrow-rich ossobuco and white-jacketed waiters at Pioneer Square's Italian standby since 1984.
il-terrazzo-carmine.blurb: Order the ossobuco, a thick veal shank over buttered fettuccine, after a plate from the antipasto bar. Carmine Smeraldo opened it in 1984.

indi-chocolate.pullQuote: Chocolate lovers should stop here for bars made from the bean up.
indi-chocolate.blurb: In the market, Indi Chocolate makes its own chocolate from scratch and sells bars and other treats at the counter.

indigo-cow.pullQuote: The plain Hokkaido milk soft serve is all you need, though toppings help.
indigo-cow.blurb: Wallingford's Indigo Cow builds its soft serve around milk from Hokkaido, and the result is gently sweet and remarkably light. Expect a line down the block in any weather. It's great unadorned, but a dip of Theo dark chocolate or brown sugar syrup with roasted soybean powder is worth adding.

inside-passage.pullQuote: Ube-and-rum Four Boys tiki drinks under fake tentacles, hidden inside Rumba.
inside-passage.blurb: Order The Four Boys, an ube and rice milk rum drink, and a plate of coconut shrimp. Book ahead; seatings last about 90 minutes.

island-soul-restaurant.pullQuote: Leave work early for rum punch, gumbo, and a coconut corn muffin.
island-soul-restaurant.blurb: Island Soul Restaurant brings lively Caribbean energy to Columbia City, with soccer on the TVs and wide windows open to the street. Fill the table with creamy mac and cheese, sticky wings, and glossy gumbo. Don't skip the coconut corn muffin, and expect one rum punch to turn into two. The kitchen also stays open late.

ivar-s.pullQuote: Alder-smoked salmon on the Lake Union deck is the plate that matters.
ivar-s.blurb: The Wallingford Ivar's faces Lake Union, and alder-smoked salmon justifies stopping at take a deck table. Clam chowder can sit beside it. Come for the water without making a ferry out of dinner.

jack-s-bbq.pullQuote: Get the pulled chicken sandwich with slaw plus a bowl of queso mac.
jack-s-bbq.blurb: The South Lake Union outpost of Jack's BBQ outshines the SoDo original, and it's easy to find a table even at lunch. The room has a laid-back honky-tonk feel. Order a barbecue-sauced pulled chicken sandwich topped with slaw, with queso mac and cheese alongside.

jackalope-tex-mex-cantina.pullQuote: Head here for tacos when Columbia City calls for Tex-Mex.
jackalope-tex-mex-cantina.blurb: Tacos and Tex-Mex plates explain the wait at Jackalope Tex-Mex & Cantina in Columbia City.

japonessa-sushi-cocina.pullQuote: Come for pico-topped rolls and sukiyaki tacos when you want a flashy dinner.
japonessa-sushi-cocina.blurb: Japonessa Sushi Cocina mixes sushi with Latin flavors, so rolls get salsa and tortillas get filled with beef sukiyaki. It's loud, touristy, and busy even midweek, but the fish is reliably good. Happy hour and a late kitchen make it an easy Downtown call.

jebena-cafe.pullQuote: Order the green lamb alongside a bowl of curried cabbage.
jebena-cafe.blurb: Lime-green walls and warm service set the tone at Jebena Cafe, an inexpensive Ethiopian spot in Lake City. The Jebena combo comes on a huge platter with several meats, vegetable sides, and house-made ayib. The best thing on the menu is the green lamb, tender and loaded with herbs and collards, and it's even better next to the curried cabbage.

joe-z-bayside-market-cafe.pullQuote: Order the smashburger, because the homemade bun is the real star.
joe-z-bayside-market-cafe.blurb: Joe'z Bayside Market + Cafe took over the old Little Market space with Oklahoma-style smashburgers plus breakfast sandwiches in the bodega mold. Everything rides on the buttery, brioche-like house bun. The burger is the move, thanks to crusty patties, tangles of blackened onion, and a lemony garlic aioli. There are still a few shelves of crackers and wine, plus roomy tables for sharing fries.

joey-university-village.pullQuote: Use this one for a late dinner after a U Village shopping run.
joey-university-village.blurb: JOEY University Village serves New American food by campus and keeps going late.

joie-coffee.pullQuote: Try a matcha latte with banana foam, which tastes better than it sounds.
joie-coffee.blurb: A pink La Marzocco anchors the counter at Joie Coffee, a tiny Ballard cafe obsessed with creamy toppings. Banana cream on iced matcha or brownie batter foam on a mocha sounds sugary, but the drinks stay surprisingly balanced. Purists can order a strong Vietnamese coffee, though the tiramisu and strawberry foams are more fun.

joule.pullQuote: Skip the usual steakhouse script and order the kalbi short rib.
joule.blurb: Joule takes the steakhouse formula and runs it through a Korean lens in Wallingford. Kalbi short rib stands in for the usual steak, sides include rice cakes tossed with chorizo and bitter mustard greens, and the bread basket gives way to scallion pancakes topped with salmon roe. Blue Victorian wallpaper and a great patio make it a strong pick for date night or dinner with parents.

kajiken.pullQuote: Skip the broth and go all in on a bowl of saucy aburasoba.
kajiken.blurb: Kajiken specializes in aburasoba, a brothless style of ramen where springy noodles get tossed in a rich sauce at the bottom of the bowl. The Capitol Hill shop keeps things casual.

kamonegi.pullQuote: When nobody can decide on dinner, soba and tempura settle the argument.
kamonegi.blurb: Fremont's Kamonegi ends dinner indecision fast with a pairing of soba and tempura that's hard to beat. The noodles are made by hand, the tempura is crisp, and after a long day of choices it feels good to let the kitchen lead. Book it for a low-key date night.

kangaroo-kiwi.pullQuote: Aussie meat pies, rugby and a raised Ballard patio in an old library.
kangaroo-kiwi.blurb: Order the pie, beans, chips and gravy, an Aussie meat pie with Heinz beans, and take it to the raised patio over Market Street. Rugby and Premier League are on the screens.

katsu-ya.pullQuote: Keep this casual Japanese spot in mind when you're around South Lake Union.
katsu-ya.blurb: Katsu-ya brings Japanese cooking to South Lake Union.

kitchen-market.pullQuote: Grab a cheap early breakfast here before the market crowds arrive.
kitchen-market.blurb: Opening early with inexpensive cafe fare, Kitchen & Market doubles as a small grocery inside Pike Place Market.

kobuta-and-ookami.pullQuote: Order the tomato and mozzarella katsu for an extremely cheesy pork cutlet.
kobuta-and-ookami.blurb: Katsu is the entire focus at Kobuta and Ookami, a Capitol Hill spot with plenty of ways to customize your cutlet. Curry katsu comes with a choice of kurobuta or iberico pork, and miso katsu works with shrimp or chicken. The standout wraps thin pork tenderloin around tomato and a heroic amount of melted mozzarella. Every set arrives with miso soup, pickles, and sesame seeds you grind yourself.

koko-s-restaurant-and-tequila-bar.pullQuote: Come late for tacos and a tequila list that keeps Capitol Hill up.
koko-s-restaurant-and-tequila-bar.blurb: Koko's Restaurant and Tequila Bar serves tacos and Mexican plates on Capitol Hill.

kona-kitchen.pullQuote: Order the kalua pig and cabbage, and get it in a quesadilla.
kona-kitchen.blurb: Maple Leaf's Kona Kitchen feels like a roadside stop on Oahu, with island memorabilia on the walls and squishy booths to sink into. The mai tais are strong, the spam musubi is reliable, and the loco moco comes smothered in gravy with your pick of rice and protein. Smoky kalua pig with cabbage is the real highlight, and the kitchen runs from breakfast through late night.

konvene-coffee-cafe.pullQuote: Hide out upstairs with a latte and the bacon, egg, and Beecher's sandwich.
konvene-coffee-cafe.blurb: Konvene Coffee Cafe is tucked upstairs inside a QFC. The baristas are friendly and steam milk beautifully. Seating is limited and there are no outlets, so plan on a short work session. Hungry visitors should order the bacon and egg sandwich with Beecher's cheese and aioli on brioche.

l-oursin.pullQuote: Order the steak frites and let the server describe the wine.
l-oursin.blurb: L'Oursin pairs a Wes Anderson palette with a playful streak, but this Central District French restaurant cooks seriously. Raw scallops and the fish of the day nod to its seafood roots, while panisse with harissa dip keeps things unpredictable. The steak frites is great, and the witty wine notes make choosing a bottle part of the fun.

la-fontana-siciliana.pullQuote: Mushroom fettuccine beside the Belltown courtyard fountain, since 1994.
la-fontana-siciliana.blurb: Order the fettuccine ai funghi, the best seller, or the squid-ink linguine with salmon. There's been a table by the courtyard fountain since 1994.

la-loba.pullQuote: Salmon candy montaditos and Barcelona tapas at 1 Hotel.
la-loba.blurb: Start with the smoked salmon candy montadito, with truffle cream cheese and local honey. Chef Oscar Amador Edo cooked at El Bulli.

la-marea.pullQuote: Order the ahi tostada with salsa macha and a crisp saison.
la-marea.blurb: Running a Mexican seafood kitchen inside Fair Isle Brewing, La Marea proves brewery food can go well beyond burgers. Crunchy tostadas lead the menu, especially the one stacked with buttery ahi and fiery salsa macha. Pair it with a farmhouse saison to tame the heat.

la-palmera.pullQuote: Grab tacos at La Palmera when South Lake Union wants something with salsa.
la-palmera.blurb: La Palmera serves tacos and other Mexican staples in South Lake Union.

la-parisienne-french-bakery.pullQuote: Get a croissant and peel it apart like a cinnamon roll.
la-parisienne-french-bakery.blurb: Belltown's La Parisienne French Bakery makes plenty of tarts and pastries, but the croissants deserve your full attention. Their thick layers unravel in spirals, with a light yeasty flavor, gentle sweetness, and a toasty, sturdy base. It's inexpensive and opens early, so it fits a regular morning routine.

lady-jaye.pullQuote: Start with the crispy pork balls and a pimento cheese cream puff.
lady-jaye.blurb: Lady Jaye takes West Seattle barbecue in unexpected directions, from panko-fried pulled pork balls to sandwiches piled with house bologna. Pastrami is made from pork collar, sausage goes into a creole dirty rice, and pimento cheese gets piped into cream puffs. Even the cocktails get creative with things like pumpkin seed orgeat. It's open late and works for brunch or a dinner with parents.

lark.pullQuote: Treat this as a backup plan, not your first choice for a big night.
lark.blurb: Expect a pleasant but forgettable evening at Lark, an upscale New American standby with a fairly bland dining room. The menu runs through familiar territory like fresh pasta, steak, crudo, and seasonal sorbet. The bolognese is fine, the raw tuna is just raw tuna, and the bread basket is hit or miss. Keep it in your back pocket rather than leading with it.

layers.pullQuote: Honestly, everything is good here, but my favorite is the TBR (turkey, bacon, ranch). Pro tip: get the spuds on the side.
layers.blurb: Honestly, everything is good here, but my favorite is the TBR (turkey, bacon, ranch). Pro tip: get the spuds on the side.

le-caviste.pullQuote: Sit at the bar with champagne and a board of charcuterie.
le-caviste.blurb: When you want Paris without the flight, Le Caviste delivers a candlelit bar, a glass of bubbly, and excellent cured meats. It suits a quick bite before a date or a solo unwind after a rough workday. The bar pours past eleven.

le-coin.pullQuote: Get the eggs benedict and a round of mini apple fritters.
le-coin.blurb: Fremont's Le Coin handles a celebratory brunch or a natural wine daytime date with ease. The eggs benedict with smoky ham, crispy potatoes, and mustard seed hollandaise is essential, as are the little apple fritters. The breakfast sandwich with pork belly, arugula, pepperoncini, radish, and fried eggs on a seedy bun is also excellent.

le-panier.pullQuote: Almond croissants and pain au chocolat, baked fresh on-site every day at Pike Place.
le-panier.blurb: Get the amandine, the almond croissant, and a pain au chocolat, the two bestsellers. Everything is baked on-site, so come early.

le-pichet.pullQuote: Linger over a slow lunch of roast chicken, charcuterie, and frites.
le-pichet.blurb: Steps from the Pike Place frenzy, Le Pichet is a calm French bistro escape. It suits a long lunch, a solo dinner, or any moment the market crowds start wearing you down. Settle in and order cured pork, roast chicken, and a pile of fries.

lenox.pullQuote: Bring the parents to Belltown for a Latin American dinner.
lenox.blurb: Lenox serves Latin American food in Belltown, and it works well for a meal with your folks.

life-on-mars.pullQuote: Come for the vinyl wall then linger over a late cocktail.
life-on-mars.blurb: Thousands of records line the walls at Life on Mars, a Capitol Hill cocktail bar where the music matters as much as the drinks. The bar runs late, so it's an easy final stop.

lil-red-s.pullQuote: Get takeout from Lil Red's when the week calls for Jamaican comfort food.
lil-red-s.blurb: Lil Red's in Columbia City cooks Jamaican barbecue and soul food that works as a reset button on a stressful week. Every plate from this kitchen leans hard into comfort, and it's still a top takeout pick. It opens early, too.

lioness.pullQuote: Stand at the marble bar with a bergamot spritz and a few snacks.
lioness.blurb: Phinney Ridge's Lioness turns Italian aperitivo hour into an actual event. The narrow room glows with tea lights and a pair of chandeliers, and the soundtrack runs as fast as the date night chatter. Folks crowd the standing marble counter over bergamot spritzes, zero-proof garibaldis, and spotless martinis.

little-jaye.pullQuote: Order the egg sandwich on brioche, but bring a fork and napkins.
little-jaye.blurb: The team behind Lady Jaye shows off its pastry skills at Little Jaye in South Park. Look for moist lemon loaf, miso chocolate chip cookies, and fluffy shokupan that disappears early. The breakfast sandwich, built on brioche with smashed sausage, a hash brown, and a runny yolk, is great and gloriously messy.

local-tide.pullQuote: Order the belly dip with house chips first, then a crab roll.
local-tide.blurb: Local Tide makes a case for Seattle seafood beyond salmon and chowder, though it nails those too. At this Fremont counter, the smoked belly dip with thin, house-seasoned chips is a must. Sandwiches are the main event, from the weekend crab roll with lemon mayo and chives to a dover sole take on the Filet-O-Fish. Shrimp toast with pork fat and a happy hour make it easy to come back.

locus-wines.pullQuote: Stop in for a pour of red before dinner in Pioneer Square.
locus-wines.blurb: Pioneer Square wine drinkers can settle in at Locus Wines.

lola.pullQuote: Order the doughnuts with mascarpone for the table and break the ice.
lola.blurb: Lola brings Greek cooking to Belltown in a room that lands right between casual and upscale, which makes it ideal for having a new partner meet your parents. Brunch calls for the seasonal scramble, and dinner calls for the lamb burger. Then get the cinnamon doughnuts, which come with vanilla bean mascarpone and a fruit compote, and eat one in a single bite.

lonely-siren.pullQuote: Head up to the rooftop for a late drink above Pike Place.
lonely-siren.blurb: Lonely Siren brings Portuguese cooking to Pike Place Market, with a roof deck and a kitchen that runs late.

louie-s-deli.pullQuote: Bacon, egg and cheese on a poppy seed bagel.
louie-s-deli.blurb: The Good Shape Pizza team turned its attention to sandwiches at Louie's Deli, a royal blue counter in Pioneer Square. Sesame hoagie rolls are crunchy and chewy, bacon is chopped into small bits, and cold cuts are shaved impossibly thin. The bacon, egg and cheese is on a poppy seed bagel. There's an arcade room next door for pinball after lunch.

lowrider-cookie-company.pullQuote: Pick up a box of cookies and an ice cream treat on your way home.
lowrider-cookie-company.blurb: Cookies and ice cream are the business at Lowrider Cookie Company in the Central District.

ltd-edition.pullQuote: Splurge on the omakase and do not skip the sake pairing.
ltd-edition.blurb: Seattle has no shortage of exclusive omakase counters, but LTD Edition on Capitol Hill deserves priority. The highlight is the uni cart, which delivers a rich sea urchin hand roll like a treat from a street vendor. Chefs explain the story behind every piece, and the sake pairing keeps flowing all night.

ludi-s-restaurant.pullQuote: Order the purple ube pancakes and settle into a booth.
ludi-s-restaurant.blurb: Seattle mourned hard when Ludi's Restaurant closed in 2019, and the reopening a few years later felt like a homecoming. The Filipino diner now sits a couple of blocks from its old Downtown home, with the same family running the griddle and breakfast served all day. Grab a booth and get the ube pancakes, still as bright purple as ever.

luna-park-cafe.pullQuote: Bring the kids for the jukeboxes and order a breakfast pile.
luna-park-cafe.blurb: Sitting under the West Seattle Bridge, Luna Park Cafe is a longtime greasy spoon packed with kitsch, from vintage lunch boxes to a giant guitar and a creepy clown game. Families fill the booths on weekends, with jukeboxes at the tables to keep kids busy. The food is plainer than the decor, but the breakfast piles are a satisfying bet.

lupo.pullQuote: Get a pizza, but make sure someone orders the sausage rigatoni.
lupo.blurb: Fremont's Lupo bakes sourdough pies in a Neapolitan oven, so the crusts come out leopard-spotted with extra chew and tang. Purists can go for the margherita with Samish Bay mozzarella, while the cacio e pepe pie is better with the pancetta add-on. The kitchen makes just one pasta, a creamy tomato rigatoni with sausage, and it's spectacular.

ma-ono.pullQuote: Order the fried chicken sandwich and a side of kimchi mac and cheese.
ma-ono.blurb: Years in, the chicken sandwich at Ma'ono in University Village still delivers. The crust is craggy, dunked in smoky pork fat and dusted with red spice, then stacked with daikon pickles and kewpie on a soft Hawaiian bun. There's a fried vegetarian patty too, and the mac and cheese with kimchi is a must.

macrina-bakery-cafe.pullQuote: Naturally leavened sourdough and pastries at the original 1993 Macrina bakery in Belltown.
macrina-bakery-cafe.blurb: Take home a loaf of the sourdough or the Rustic Potato bread, and eat a pastry with coffee here. This Belltown cafe is where Macrina began in 1993.

made-in-house.pullQuote: Order the daily bento and plan on skipping the rest of your afternoon.
made-in-house.blurb: Midafternoon on a weekday, this Fremont lunch spot is still full of people who clearly cleared their calendars. At Made in House, the bento changes daily and brings bulgogi, a jammy egg, springy japchae, and tempura kale that cracks apart at first bite. Salmon kimbop gets rolled fresh each day, and the shortbread bar tastes like a homemade candy bar.

mainstay-provisions.pullQuote: An early, inexpensive Phinney Ridge coffee stop that keeps the morning simple.
mainstay-provisions.blurb: Mainstay Provisions opens early on Phinney Ridge as a neighborhood cafe that won't cost you much.

maiz.pullQuote: Skip the seafood for once and eat fresh masa tamales at the market.
maiz.blurb: Pike Place pushes everyone toward seafood, but Maíz makes a strong case for corn instead. This bright tortilleria grinds its own nixtamal masa and presses tortillas you'll want to eat every week. That masa shows up in tacos, tamales, and chips with a serious, shattering crunch.

mamma-melina-ristorante-pizzeria.pullQuote: An easy U District pick for Italian dinner and a pizza to share.
mamma-melina-ristorante-pizzeria.blurb: Mamma Melina Ristorante + Pizzeria serves Italian plates and pizza to a U District crowd.

maneki.pullQuote: Book a tatami room, take your shoes off, and let the sake flow.
maneki.blurb: Open since before the Model T, Maneki holds the title of Seattle's oldest Japanese restaurant, and it still fills up most nights in the Chinatown-International District. Text ahead for a reservation or expect a very late seating. The main room has a lively hum, but the private tatami rooms are the real move, quiet and closed off with good sushi and plenty of sake.

many-bennies.pullQuote: Cheap scoops in Wallingford, no planning required, just show up hungry.
many-bennies.blurb: Inexpensive ice cream in Wallingford is the whole pitch at Many Bennies, and you can just walk in.

maria-luisa-empanadas.pullQuote: Order more empanadas than you think you need, especially the creamed spinach.
maria-luisa-empanadas.blurb: Over in Ballard, Maria Luisa Empanadas turns out tender pastries stuffed with meats, cheeses, and vegetables, plus a chimichurri you'll want to bottle. The garage-style room has high-tops for a quick lunch, and takeout is easy even for a crowd. Picking a favorite is hard, but the creamed spinach and the tangy chorizo lead the pack.

marination.pullQuote: Grab a patio seat at Alki and treat it like the beach shack you deserved.
marination.blurb: Think of every sad boardwalk snack bar from your childhood, then picture the opposite. That's Marination at Alki, a Hawaiian spot with a sunny patio and food that justifies the drive to West Seattle even if you live across town. Bring sunscreen if you're sitting outside.

maripili-tapas-bar.pullQuote: The best tapas in town, and the right call for a double date.
maripili-tapas-bar.blurb: Galician cooking with a light hand and real restraint is the draw at Maripili Tapas Bar on Capitol Hill.
