Expect ling cod in a sharp, tangy fish broth, manchego gnocchi, a runny-centered tortilla de patata, and garlic aioli on just about everything. Come with another couple, mark a low-key celebration, or sit solo at the bar and graze. The wine list leans Spanish and Washington.

market-at-the-park.pullQuote: Seafood up top in Belltown, best saved for a clear evening.
market-at-the-park.blurb: For seafood with rooftop seating in Belltown, MARKET at the Park is the move.

market-grill.pullQuote: Get the blackened salmon sandwich with rosemary mayo and a cup of chowder.
market-grill.blurb: Squeezing through Pike Place crowds sounds like a bad lunch plan, but Market Grill makes it pay off. The counter sits right in the middle of the action, where the cooks sear a blackened salmon sandwich slicked in rosemary mayo. Add the herby clam chowder on the side. Solo diners can usually snag a stool, while groups should take it to go.

market-house-meats.pullQuote: The corned beef reuben here is the benchmark for every deli in town.
market-house-meats.blurb: Look for the huge corned beef sign over the Denny Triangle and you've found Market House Meats. The shop has fed office workers and early construction crews since the forties, and the griddle is always sizzling. That tender, salty corned beef goes into a reuben you'll measure every other one against. It's inexpensive, quick, and open early.

marmalade.pullQuote: Order the salted graham in an affogato and forget about the weather.
marmalade.blurb: Whimsical signs out front hint at what's inside Marmalade, a Fremont gelato shop that might spoil you for the rest of the city. The gelato is spun fresh and airy, and the flavors get creative without getting silly. White chocolate tastes rich and buttery, salted graham is nutty and layered, and strawberry lemonade sorbetto is as smooth as soft serve. Go big with the Americano cup or get a scoop drowned in espresso.

mas-cafe.pullQuote: The bacon breakfast sandwich here is worth a scratch from a stray shard.
mas-cafe.blurb: A tiny roadside coffee shop in Wallingford, Mas Cafe does Mexican breakfasts and a bacon sandwich that might be the city's best. A soft Macrina bun holds a lacy fried egg, grilled onions, red chile aioli, white cheddar, and a heap of bacon cooked until it shatters. The sausage version with provolone is excellent too, and so are the breakfast burritos.

mashiko-japanese-restaurant.blurb: Mashiko Japanese Restaurant has anchored the West Seattle sushi scene for years, known for its focus on sustainably sourced fish.

matsu.pullQuote: Late-night sushi in Pioneer Square once the craving is better than bar food.
matsu.blurb: Matsu keeps its Pioneer Square sushi spot going past eleven, which is rare in this part of town.

matt-s-in-the-market.pullQuote: Book a window table upstairs and make lunch the best part of the day.
matt-s-in-the-market.blurb: Pike Place on a rainy Saturday, elbow to elbow with tourists, rarely feels romantic. Climb the stairs to Matt's in the Market and the whole thing shifts, with seafood and a window view that make the market look charming again. You are paying for the room too, so save it for a date or a lunch you want to remember.

maximilien.pullQuote: Classic French cooking and a water view, tucked away from the market crowds.
maximilien.blurb: Maximilien serves French food in Pike Place Market, with windows looking out over Elliott Bay.

mean-sandwich.pullQuote: Griddled corned beef with mint and pickled cabbage, from a Momofuku alum.
mean-sandwich.blurb: Order the Mean: thick griddled corned beef, house yellow mustard, pickled red cabbage and fresh mint on a challah bun. It comes with the salt-and-pepper potato skins.

mee-sum-pastry.pullQuote: Get the steamed barbecue pork bao and eat it walking through the stalls.
mee-sum-pastry.blurb: Swing by in the late morning, before the market fully wakes up, and you'll catch the crew at Mee Sum Pastry folding potstickers and pinching shumai. Grab an assortment and snack your way through Pike Place. It's all good, but the steamed pork hum bao is the order regulars make, and it's open early and inexpensive.

messina.pullQuote: Save this Lower Queen Anne Italian spot for your next date night.
messina.blurb: For an Italian date night by Seattle Center, Messina is a strong call.

metropolitan-grill.pullQuote: The downtown steakhouse to book when the expense account is paying.
metropolitan-grill.blurb: Metropolitan Grill has been downtown's classic steakhouse since the eighties, all dark wood, big steaks, and expense-account energy. The kitchen stays open late, so it works after a game or a show.

midnite-ramen.pullQuote: A solid Fremont noodle stop when the weather turns and you want broth.
midnite-ramen.blurb: A casual Fremont ramen shop, Midnite Ramen is an easy call for a bowl of noodles.

mike-s-noodle-house.pullQuote: Bring cash, order the brisket noodles, and add a bowl of congee.
mike-s-noodle-house.blurb: Two neon signs under the red awning spell it out, congee and noodles, and Mike's Noodle House has been nailing both for years in the CID. Springy egg noodles come loaded with tender brisket and bright greens, while the congee is thick, warm, and soothing. The small dining room hums with chatter and fast service. It's cash only, so stop at the ATM first.

milk-drunk.pullQuote: Cheap Beacon Hill ice cream that makes dessert an easy yes.
milk-drunk.blurb: On Beacon Hill, Milk Drunk scoops inexpensive ice cream for a sweet stop after dinner.

milstead-co.pullQuote: Serious coffee, communal tables, and a homemade Oreo you shouldn't skip.
milstead-co.blurb: Coffee obsessives in Fremont already know Milstead & Co. as the shop that gets every cup right. Seating is mostly communal and there's wifi, so it works for heads-down solo time or a team work session. Grab the house-made Oreo from Standard Bakery before you go.

mirabelle-by-orphee.pullQuote: An early Pioneer Square stop for French pastry on the way to work.
mirabelle-by-orphee.blurb: Mirabelle by Orphée opens early in Pioneer Square with inexpensive French pastries for the morning commute.

miss-pho.pullQuote: Order the phở hà nội and drop that raw yolk right in.
miss-pho.blurb: It looks like any strip-mall Vietnamese spot in Greenwood, but Miss Pho cooks well above the setting. Phở hà nội comes brimming with broth and topped with a raw egg yolk, great stirred in or spooned over each bite of noodles and beef shank. The grilled chicken is fragrant with lemongrass, and vegetarians eat just as well here.

molly-moon-s.pullQuote: Nutmeg-spiked cookie dough ice cream in a hot waffle cone on Capitol Hill.
molly-moon-s.blurb: Get the cookie dough, a nutmeg-scented flavor that's always on, in a fresh waffle cone. Sample freely; the line moves.

momiji-slu.pullQuote: A dependable Denny Triangle sushi stop for a weeknight roll fix.
momiji-slu.blurb: For sushi just north of the retail core without a big production, Momiji SLU is a solid pick.

mondello-italian-restaurant.pullQuote: A Magnolia Italian dinner that saves you the drive across town.
mondello-italian-restaurant.blurb: Mondello Italian Restaurant gives Magnolia a neighborhood Italian dinner option close to home.

monkey-loft.pullQuote: A SoDo dance floor for when last call feels way too early.
monkey-loft.blurb: Monkey Loft keeps the SoDo dance floor going late and well into the early hours.

monorail-espresso.pullQuote: A walk-up espresso window for a fast, cheap shot on the way in.
monorail-espresso.blurb: From a tiny walk-up window near the Denny Triangle, Monorail Espresso pulls inexpensive shots starting early.

moto-pizza.pullQuote: Square pies with crispy edges, best split with a friend in Belltown.
moto-pizza.blurb: Thick, square pies are the draw at Moto Pizza in Belltown, a casual pick for pizza night.

mountaineering-club.pullQuote: Come for the view and the Banana Pancakes cocktail, not the hot dog.
mountaineering-club.blurb: Perched on the Graduate Hotel roof by campus, Mountaineering Club does camp-lodge decor with real polish and a sweeping view east. The drinks lean into the outdoorsy theme, with the Banana Pancakes and Orange Snack leading the list. If you're eating, go for the bacon sandwich and pass on the pricey frank. Service continues after eleven.

mr-fish-chips-chowder.pullQuote: Fine for a patio break with visitors, but skip the pricey crab.
mr-fish-chips-chowder.blurb: Up at the north end of Pike Place, Mr. Fish Chips & Chowder caters to tourists with a menu that comes and goes in quality. The fried fish is fine, and the bacon-y clam chowder with its Goldfish-style crackers is the strongest play. A breezy patio over Elliott Bay makes it a decent rest stop with guests.

mr-west-cafe-bar-downtown.pullQuote: Bring the laptop, order a matcha latte, and camp out all day.
mr-west-cafe-bar-downtown.blurb: If you need somewhere to work all day without going hungry, Mr West Cafe Bar Downtown is the answer. The room is all plants, marble, and gold accents, which suits curried avocado toast and a green tea latte. Lunch brings polished panini and salads, and later on there are cheese boards and frozen wine slushies.

mt-bagel.pullQuote: Buy a bag of everything bagels and a tub of the spicy scallion schmear.
mt-bagel.blurb: Seattle's bagel scene changed when Mt. Bagel showed up selling them whole, with tubs of schmear to take home. Inside, they're malty, chewy, and a little sweet, and they hold up great frozen and toasted later. The crust's crackle can vary, but the flavor never does, especially on the garlicky everything.

musang.pullQuote: Filipino cooking on Beacon Hill worth dressing up for, parents or date in tow.
musang.blurb: Musang turns Filipino food into a full-on celebration on Beacon Hill, and you are paying for the room too. Bring a date or bring the folks, and order plenty to share.

my-friend-derek-s.blurb: Wallingford gets solid pizza from My Friend Derek’s, a neighborhood spot for a casual dinner.

mykonos-greek-grill.pullQuote: Order the chicken lemon rice soup and an overstuffed gyro, nothing more needed.
mykonos-greek-grill.blurb: Near Green Lake, Mykonos Greek Grill turns out Greek food that punches well above its casual setup. The falafel is crisp and nicely seasoned, the avgolemono is pure comfort, and the gyro comes stuffed to bursting. Grab a table or take a spread of mezze to go for a picnic.

nana-s-green-tea.pullQuote: Order the matcha parfait with cake on top and call it lunch.
nana-s-green-tea.blurb: After a rough morning, sometimes the fix is sitting alone with soft serve in a waffle cone crowned with a whole slice of cake. Nana's Green Tea, a matcha-everything Japanese cafe downtown, is happy to make that your midday meal.

neb.blurb: For a glass of wine in Belltown that feels like a step up from the usual bar, Neb is a smart pick.

needle-and-thread.pullQuote: Skip the menu, name a spirit you like, and let the bartender decide.
needle-and-thread.blurb: Getting into Needle and Thread is half the fun. Book online, walk through Tavern Law, pick up an old phone in the corner, and wait for someone to lead you up a creaky staircase to a vintage parlor. There's no drink list, so tell the bartenders your preferences and they'll build something around them. It's easier to land a seat than you'd think, and it runs late.

neko.pullQuote: Capitol Hill coffee with a side of cats who may or may not like you.
neko.blurb: Neko lets you sip something warm while hanging out with cats on Capitol Hill, and it's inexpensive and open early.

nick-s-on-madison.pullQuote: A Madison Park neighborhood dinner when you would rather not leave the area.
nick-s-on-madison.blurb: Madison Park neighbors have Nick's on Madison for New American cooking close to home.

nielsens-pastries.pullQuote: Order a Snitter, then grab marzipan almond cake for someone you love.
nielsens-pastries.blurb: Everyone comes to this cheerful Danish bakery for the Snitter, a pastry that tastes like a cinnamon roll crossed with a cheese danish. Nielsens Pastries has been at it in Lower Queen Anne for decades, and the case explains why. The marzipan almond cake is a birthday-worthy dessert you'll probably start eating on the drive home.

nikko-teriyaki.pullQuote: The best teriyaki chicken in West Seattle is worth every extra minute.
nikko-teriyaki.blurb: Expect a slightly longer wait at Nikko Teriyaki, because the chicken here is cooked low and slow. It lands somewhere between grilled and braised, with a beautiful sear, a gingery sauce, and a salad dressed with a sour-apple kick. Nobody in West Seattle does it better.

nue.pullQuote: Bring a group to brunch and order the Sichuan wings for the table.
nue.blurb: Street food from all over the map shares one menu on Capitol Hill, from Burmese and Jamaican to South African and Chinese. It should be a mess, but Nue makes every detour land. Weekend mornings here swap the benedict for tocino and fried rice, harissa-laced octopus, and pineapple-coconut cornbread. A pile of crunchy Sichuan wings never hurts either.

oddfellows-cafe-and-bar.pullQuote: Order the soft herby scrambled eggs and a latte, then linger awhile.
oddfellows-cafe-and-bar.blurb: Equal parts French bistro, espresso counter, and old-fashioned grocery, Oddfellows Café and Bar leans hard into exposed brick and Capitol Hill cool. Come early for coffee and soft scrambled eggs with cheese and herbs, or show up later for cocktails on the patio or a relaxed dinner date. There are no reservations, and weekend brunch is busier than dinner, so have a backup in mind.

off-alley.pullQuote: A Columbia City splurge for a date who appreciates serious cooking.
off-alley.blurb: Off Alley packs a lot of ambition into a tiny Columbia City room, and this is a dressed-up night that makes sense for a date night.

old-stove-brewing.pullQuote: House beers and plenty of tables when your whole crew hits the market.
old-stove-brewing.blurb: In the market, Old Stove Brewing pours its own beer and has room for a big group.

oliver-s-lounge.pullQuote: A classic downtown hotel lounge for a cold martini and quiet conversation.
oliver-s-lounge.blurb: Inside the Mayflower Park Hotel downtown, Oliver's Lounge has a long reputation for its martinis. Big windows look out on the street, and it's a calm spot for a drink after shopping.

olympia-coffee.pullQuote: A sharp downtown espresso stop for people who actually care about the beans.
olympia-coffee.blurb: Downtown commuters get an early start with Olympia Coffee and its well-regarded roasts.

ooink.pullQuote: Come solo or as a pair for the tenderest chashu in town.
ooink.blurb: Capitol Hill has no shortage of ramen, but Ooink earns its spot with the most tender sliced pork around and some seriously oversized gyoza. The room is small, so plan on going alone or with one friend. It's the bowl you want when you've got a cold.

oriental-mart.pullQuote: Order the salmon sinigang, follow the signs, and don't rush the cook.
oriental-mart.blurb: In a quiet corner of Pike Place Market, a Filipino counter is wallpapered with handwritten signs pinned up by clothespins, each one warning you to behave. They seem gruff at first and get funnier the longer you read. Oriental Mart backs up the attitude with the best lunch in the market and some of the city's finest Filipino cooking. You can get in before work and won't cost much.

otherside-market-deli.pullQuote: Get the Italian sub, add a breakfast sandwich, and bring patience.
otherside-market-deli.blurb: The owners once ran Lyon's Grocery in Queen Anne, and that pedigree shows in every sandwich at Otherside Market & Deli in Eastlake. The Italian sub piles on ham with pepperoncini and a hit of red wine vinegar, while breakfast sandwiches arrive gooey on Backyard bagels. Even a plain turkey and cheese on wheat is great here.

otherworld.pullQuote: Natural wine nerds, this is your clubhouse, deep cuts and murky pours included.
otherworld.blurb: Remember the Juice Club pop-up? Its crew now runs Otherworld, a Capitol Hill natural wine bar built for glou-glou devotees. Prices hang on a deli-style felt board, the shelves are lined with bottles sporting arty labels, and the music runs funky and obscure. Settle in with small glasses of something cloudy, and know the night runs long here.

ox-burger.pullQuote: A cheap Central District burger fix you can grab at the counter.
ox-burger.blurb: Inexpensive burgers from a casual counter make Ox Burger an easy Central District stop.

oxbow.pullQuote: Eat the garlic bagel with Calabrian chili cream cheese within the hour.
oxbow.blurb: The team behind Sea Wolf runs Oxbow in Montlake, and the bagels live up to that reputation. They have a crackly, shell-like crust, a dense chew, and a gentle sour tang, but they go stale fast, so eat them right away. With wifi, good smells from the ovens, and a late-afternoon close, it makes a fine daytime hangout.

paju.pullQuote: Start with the seafood pancake and a chili lime martini, then keep ordering.
paju.blurb: Paju traded its cramped Queen Anne home for a much bigger South Lake Union space with a full bar, a wood-fired grill anchoring the open kitchen, and plenty of black marble. The menu grew too, but the reasons to come are the same ones as before. A savory seafood pancake buried in wiggling bonito flakes goes great with the chili lime oil martini, and squid-ink kimchi fried rice comes with bacon. Bring a special-occasion budget.

palace-kitchen.pullQuote: Goat cheese and lavender fondue and a Palace Burger Royale at Tom Douglas's late bar.
palace-kitchen.blurb: Order the goat cheese-lavender fondue with apples and grilled focaccia, then the Palace Burger Royale. Grab a stool at the big bar in Belltown.

pancita.pullQuote: Come to Ravenna for tacos that are worth a detour across town.
pancita.blurb: Mexican cooking comes to Ravenna at Pancita, and the tacos are the reason to go.

paper-fan-cocktail-bar.pullQuote: Order the Lychee Blossom and bring a first date up to the loft.
paper-fan-cocktail-bar.blurb: Most trips to Biang Biang Noodles end face-first in a bowl of mala beef, but look up next time. Behind red velvet curtains sits Paper Fan Cocktail Bar, a snug loft dressed with ornate lamps and delicate fans. A few of the tea-based drinks lean medicinal, though the Lychee Blossom, made with gin, green tea, and lemon, drinks bright and easy. It fills up fast, so reserve ahead for a first date.

paseo.pullQuote: Order the Caribbean Roast and grab extra napkins, you will need them.
paseo.blurb: Seattle's most famous sandwich might be the Caribbean Roast at Paseo, a pile of marinated roast pork and caramelized onions on a toasted baguette. It's gloriously messy, so eat it right away in Fremont rather than letting it sit.

pasta-casalinga.pullQuote: Get the pomodoro with burrata and leave space for the ricotta crostata.
pasta-casalinga.blurb: Inside Pike Place Market, Pasta Casalinga turns out handmade bowls that would hold their own in Italy. The rotating menu pulls from ocean, garden, and farm, think rigatoni with lamb and juniper ragu or spaghettoni tossed in kale pesto. The best bowl is the simplest one, pomodoro topped with a cool spoonful of burrata. If the ricotta chocolate crostata is on, order it, and bring your parents.

percy-s-and-co.blurb: In Ballard, Percy's and Co. keeps the cocktails coming past eleven.

petit-pierre-bakery.pullQuote: A Magnolia morning stop for buttery French pastry on the cheap.
petit-pierre-bakery.blurb: Magnolia mornings start early at Petit Pierre Bakery, with inexpensive French pastries and bread.

petoskey-s-sports-bar.pullQuote: Fremont's go-to for watching the game with a big, loud group.
petoskey-s-sports-bar.blurb: Bring the whole crew to Petoskey's Sports Bar in Fremont for the game, bar food, and a late close.

pho-bac.pullQuote: Order the short rib bowl and ask about the half-chicken special.
pho-bac.blurb: Not every night calls for a dress code, and Phở Bắc in the CID is proof. The vibe is casual and cool, the menu runs from phở to Vietnamese drinking snacks, and parking is actually easy. Brisket and meatball bowls are great, but the huge short rib version and the occasional off-menu bowl with a whole poached half-chicken are the stars.

pick-quick-drive-in.pullQuote: Eat a double cheeseburger and a root beer float in the car.
pick-quick-drive-in.blurb: For a double cheeseburger with fries and a shake on pocket change, Pick-Quick Drive In has you covered. The burgers beat Dick's handily, and you get to sit down while you eat them. Load your friends into the car and get everyone root beer floats made with real soft serve.

pike-place-chowder.pullQuote: New England clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl, with oyster crackers, in Post Alley.
pike-place-chowder.blurb: Get the clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl and add oyster crackers. Skip the smoked salmon chowder.

pike-place-market.pullQuote: Go early on a weekday, graze the stalls, and watch the fish fly.
pike-place-market.blurb: Seattle's famous public market opens early, and a weekday morning is the best time to wander before the crowds arrive. Pike Place Market rewards grazing, with produce, flowers, baked goods, and seafood counters at every turn.

pink-salt.pullQuote: A Magnolia option for Peruvian food when you want something beyond the usual.
pink-salt.blurb: For Peruvian food without leaving Magnolia, Pink Salt is the neighborhood answer.

piroshky-piroshky.pullQuote: Get the beef and cheese, eat it standing up, and don't mind the line.
piroshky-piroshky.blurb: Since the early nineties, Piroshky Piroshky has filled the market with the smell of baked Russian hand pies, both savory and sweet. The line moves faster than it looks, prices stay friendly, and the counter opens early enough to make breakfast out of a smoked salmon pastry.

pizza-by-ruffin.pullQuote: Roman-style squares this crunchy are reason enough to rethink your weekday lunch.
pizza-by-ruffin.blurb: Tucked into a slim corner of an office-tower food court, Pizza by Ruffin sells al taglio slabs with a serious crackle. The margherita and the pepperoni are dependable, but the fun is in the odd ones, like mushroom lit up with green Jamaican curry or squash paired with brie. South Lake Union has never had much good pizza, so this counts as real progress.

place-pigalle-restaurant-and-bar.pullQuote: Book a window table at sunset and let the Sound do half the romancing.
place-pigalle-restaurant-and-bar.blurb: Down a flight of stairs at the back of the market, Place Pigalle Restaurant and Bar hides a small French dining room with big windows over Elliott Bay. The check is a special-occasion one, but the view, the quiet, and the French cooking make a date night feel planned well in advance.

pono-ranch.pullQuote: Hawaiian bar food and a kitchen open past eleven make an easy Ballard nightcap.
pono-ranch.blurb: Hawaiian plates and a late-running kitchen make Pono Ranch a handy stop on any Ballard bar crawl.

portage-bay-cafe.pullQuote: Bring the whole brunch crew, picky eaters and toddlers included, and nobody leaves unhappy.
portage-bay-cafe.blurb: When a weekend brunch involves ten people with ten opinions, Portage Bay Cafe is the safe call. The menu is enormous, the ingredients lean local, and pancakes or french toast come with access to a toppings bar piled with fruit and whipped cream. You can even skip the plate entirely and just graze the bar.

post-alley-pizza.pullQuote: Grab a charred, chewy slice and shake on more garlic than seems reasonable.
post-alley-pizza.blurb: Ignore the name, because Post Alley Pizza isn't actually in the market. It's a dependable downtown lunch slice with a crust that manages to be both blistered and chewy, plus dipping sauces like house ranch and a Calabrian chili buffalo. The real perk is a shaker of granulated garlic, which almost no other slice shop in town bothers to put out.

project-9-brewing-co.pullQuote: Wild sours, hazy IPAs, and a pastrami truck out front settle every group debate.
project-9-brewing-co.blurb: The tap list here swings from peanut butter and jelly sours to turtle stout to fruit-loaded IPAs, so nobody needs a plan. A big patio sits on a busy Maple Leaf corner and makes for a long, summery session. For food, the Sammich truck parked outside does a pastrami sandwich that's the move. When friends are coming from opposite ends of the city, meet at Project 9 Brewing Co.

pufftown-bakehouse.pullQuote: An early pastry stop for market wanderers who want something flaky and cheap.
pufftown-bakehouse.blurb: Inexpensive pastries and an early opening make Pufftown Bakehouse an easy first stop on a Pike Place Market morning.

purple-cafe-and-wine-bar.pullQuote: Lobster mac and cheese beside a 30-foot tower of wine near Benaroya Hall.
purple-cafe-and-wine-bar.blurb: Order the Maine lobster mac and cheese and a glass from the long list. The wine tower anchors the room; happy hour runs weekdays 2 to 5.

queen-anne-beerhall.pullQuote: Long communal tables and liters of German beer make group nights easy.
queen-anne-beerhall.blurb: Near Seattle Center, Queen Anne Beerhall is a roomy German-style beer hall with shared tables and plenty of space for a crowd. That early drink deal is a solid deal, and the bar keeps pouring well past eleven, which helps after a game or concert next door.

queen-mary-tea-room.pullQuote: For a proper afternoon tea with all the frills, start your search here.
queen-mary-tea-room.blurb: Ravenna's Queen Mary Tea Room goes all in on the ritual, with aproned servers passing around tea samples and decor that changes with the seasons. Tiered trays come loaded with things like tiny cups of tomato bisque plus fresh fruit for dragging through clotted cream. There's a gluten-free version that holds its own, and the tea list is huge.

rachel-s-bagels-burritos.pullQuote: Indecisive mornings end well here, since the bagels and burritos are both excellent.
rachel-s-bagels-burritos.blurb: The name tells you the plan, and Rachel's Bagels & Burritos delivers on both halves. Bagels come chewy with a crackly shell, great under a thick smear of cream cheese and some everything-seasoned chile crisp. Burritos are stuffed with roasted potato chunks and fillings like celery root al pastor or maitake mushrooms.

rachel-s-ginger-beer.pullQuote: Duck in for a spiked mule when the market crowds get to be too much.
rachel-s-ginger-beer.blurb: After a couple of hours dodging tourists at Pike Place, Rachel's Ginger Beer is a welcome breather. The house ginger beer comes plain or in flavors like pink guava and cucumber tarragon, and any of them can be turned into a boozy mule. It's cheap, it's open late, and it's right in the middle of everything.

radiator-whiskey.pullQuote: Order the pork belly burnt ends and a whiskey, then stay for another round.
radiator-whiskey.blurb: Climb the stairs above the market and you'll find Radiator Whiskey, a small, dark room with a deep whiskey list and food built to absorb it. Think burnt ends, tots smothered in gravy with a fried egg, and marrow bones set up for a luge. Reserve ahead for the smoked pig's head, though landing a table on a Friday is usually painless.

rainier-teriyaki.pullQuote: This is the teriyaki to settle any argument about the city's signature takeout.
rainier-teriyaki.blurb: Teriyaki is a Seattle invention, and Rainier Teriyaki in Mount Baker is the standard everyone else gets measured against. The chicken comes off the grill with a smoky char and a glaze that caramelizes on the edges. Little touches seal it, like iceberg salad packed on the side so it stays crisp, blistered gingery gyoza, and extra sauce tucked in without asking. Takeout comes together fast without slipping.

ramen-danbo.pullQuote: Go thin and firm on the noodles, extra rich on the broth.
ramen-danbo.blurb: Expect a line at Ramen DANBO, and expect it to be worth it for Hakata-style tonkotsu this good. The order sheet lets you dial in noodle firmness, broth richness, and spice, so ask for extra fat plus extra karadare if you want it silky and hot. Plenty of counter seats make it an easy solo dinner.

re-public.pullQuote: Call here when you need a last-minute birthday table for a dozen friends.
re-public.blurb: The menu at Re:public dresses up comfort food, with burgers, Nashville hot chicken sandwiches, and mac and cheese loaded with prawns and pork belly. It's more about the mood than the cooking, especially in summer when the garage doors roll up. Groups can usually claim a section of the bar with little notice, the kitchen stays open late, and there's a happy hour too.

red-mill-burgers.pullQuote: Get onion rings to dunk in fry sauce, plus a mint truffle shake.
red-mill-burgers.blurb: Nobody comes to Red Mill Burgers for gourmet toppings or atmosphere. You come for a charbroiled diner-style patty, cornmeal-crusted onion rings dunked in fry sauce, and a thick shake in flavors like s'mores. Grab a spot at one of the bright red picnic tables, ideally after a hike or a slow afternoon around Phinney Ridge.

rob-roy.pullQuote: Settle into a dark corner and order something stirred, strong, and classic.
rob-roy.blurb: A dark, grown-up Belltown bar, Rob Roy takes cocktails seriously without getting precious about them. Happy hour is the smart way in, and the bartenders are as comfortable with the classics as with their own inventions.

rockcreek-seafood-spirits.pullQuote: Grab a seat on the roof deck and make happy hour a seafood dinner.
rockcreek-seafood-spirits.blurb: Fremont's RockCreek Seafood & Spirits is a lively seafood house with a long menu of fish and shellfish and a solid cocktail list. Happy hour draws a crowd, and when the weather cooperates, the rooftop is where you want to be.

rojo-s-mexican-food.pullQuote: Vegan tortas this good might convert the most committed carnitas fan at lunch.
rojo-s-mexican-food.blurb: Everything at Rojo’s Mexican Food is plant-based, though you'd hardly guess from a menu of asada, chicken, and carnitas-style fillings made in-house. Strong marinades do the heavy lifting, and the jackfruit is a convincing stand-in for braised pork. The small, bright room in Pioneer Square works for a quick lunch with coworkers or a burrito to carry into a Mariners game.

roma-roma.pullQuote: Come for crunchy al taglio squares, linger over a lambrusco granita and an old movie.
roma-roma.blurb: On Capitol Hill, Roma Roma cuts thick, crisp al taglio slabs and sells them by weight. Toppings range from pepperoni cups to wild boar bolognese, and not all of them land, but the room makes up for it with wild floor tiles and classic Hollywood films projected overhead. It's easy to drop in any time, ideally when a musical is on.

rondo-japanese.pullQuote: Keep this Capitol Hill sushi spot in mind for an easy weeknight dinner.
rondo-japanese.blurb: Sushi is the focus at Rondo Japanese, a Japanese spot on Capitol Hill.

roquette.pullQuote: French-spirit cocktails from Erik Hakkinen on First Ave.
roquette.blurb: Erik Hakkinen's Belltown bar leans on cognac and calvados, and it's open until 1 or 2am every night.

rosellini-s.pullQuote: Order the croissant, then come back tomorrow for another one.
rosellini-s.blurb: The morning line at Rosellini's tells you everything about where Ballard gets its pastry. The baguette and cinnamon-swirled coffee cake are excellent, but the croissant is the reason to come, with shattering layers, deep butter flavor, and a crumb that springs back when you press it. Get there early, since the doors open before nine.

royal-grinders.pullQuote: Split the Italian with a friend, or don't, and grab a bag of chips.
royal-grinders.blurb: Proper East Coast-style subs are rare in Seattle, which makes Royal Grinders in Fremont a real asset. The Italian is what you should request, stacked with pepperoni, salami, ham, provolone, swiss, and chopped pepperoncini on bread that's crisp outside and soft within, plus a ranch spread you'll want to take home. Every sandwich here is massive, so sharing is reasonable.

sabine.pullQuote: An early-morning Ballard stop for a cheap pastry and a coffee.
sabine.blurb: Open early and easy on the wallet, Sabine is a Ballard bakery and cafe for pastries and coffee.

saigon-drip-cafe.pullQuote: Different from the traditional bánh mì, but that side of beef bone marrow broth makes it uniquely amazing and a must.
saigon-drip-cafe.blurb: Different from the traditional bánh mì, but that side of beef bone marrow broth makes it uniquely amazing and a must.

saigon-viet-nam-deli.pullQuote: The grilled pork bánh mì here is still a cheap lunch miracle.
saigon-viet-nam-deli.blurb: Prices creep up everywhere, but Saigon Viet Nam Deli in the International District still sells a bánh mì that barely dents your wallet. The grilled pork version comes on crackly fresh bread with a generous swipe of bơ and plenty of coarse black pepper. It tastes the same every time, which is the highest compliment.

saint-bread.pullQuote: Order the za'atar avocado toast and a custard bun, then sit by the water.
saint-bread.blurb: Saint Bread looks like a boathouse that floated in from some faraway fishing village, stained glass and all, but it sits on the U District edge of Portage Bay. The avocado toast is a standout thanks to a heavy hand with za'atar, good olive oil, and precise lemon and salt. There's also a take on Norwegian school buns stuffed with custard and raspberry jam, made for a slow Saturday breakfast.

salt-straw.pullQuote: Expect a line, a pile of tasting spoons, and flavors you won't find elsewhere.
salt-straw.blurb: The Portland-born Salt & Straw brings its oddball, seasonal scoops to Ballard, and the counter stays open late. Staff hand out samples freely, which helps when the monthly specials get weird.

salumi.pullQuote: As the name states, go for any of their salami sandwiches and you’ll be coming back.
salumi.blurb: As the name states, go for any of their salami sandwiches and you’ll be coming back.

san-fermo.pullQuote: Bring a date here when you need dinner to go exactly as planned.
san-fermo.blurb: Some restaurants just know what you need, and San Fermo in Ballard is reliable in exactly that way. Set in a pair of old houses, the room feels warm and lived-in, and the pasta gives you a reason to come back. It's the Italian spot you book when there's no room for a dud evening.

santo-coffee-co.pullQuote: An early-opening Roosevelt coffee shop for a cheap, well-made morning cup.
santo-coffee-co.blurb: Santo Coffee Co pours coffee in Roosevelt from early morning, and it won't cost you much.

sea-wolf.pullQuote: A brown-butter chocolate chip cookie and crusty white sourdough on Stone Way.
sea-wolf.blurb: Get the chocolate chip cookie, with brown butter, oats and sea salt, plus a croissant. Take home a loaf of the white sourdough.

seafab.pullQuote: A cheap, early U District cafe with a seafood bent worth checking out.
seafab.blurb: Seafood and cafe fare share the menu at Seafab, an inexpensive U District spot that opens early.

seatangofoods.pullQuote: Come for the empanadas and leave with a box of alfajores for later.
seatangofoods.blurb: This Lake City counter is among the few places in Seattle specializing in Argentine baked goods, from dulce de leche alfajores to glossy medialunas and quince pastafrola. Still, the empanadas are why Seatangofoods deserves a lunch detour, golden and often fresh out of the oven. Lake City can get an empanada before the commute, which is the practical glory here.

seattle-biscuit-company.pullQuote: Order the Gus, with fried chicken, pickles, an egg, and sausage gravy.
seattle-biscuit-company.blurb: The Fremont room feels like a boxcar diner shrunk down by a tiny-house builder, and Seattle Biscuit Company serves breakfast all day. Biscuits anchor everything, and they are excellent, whether in a sandwich like the peanut butter, apple, and jam Lunch Pail or smothered in classic gravy. Very hungry groups can tackle a huge platter of biscuits and eggs.

seattle-dumpling-house.pullQuote: Start with the soup dumplings and let the rest of the order follow.
seattle-dumpling-house.blurb: Soup dumplings are the order at Seattle Dumpling House, a Wallingford spot for Chinese dumplings and dim sum.

seattle-fish-guys.pullQuote: Order the poke with spicy salmon and a scoop of smoky mac salad.
seattle-fish-guys.blurb: The poke at Seattle Fish Guys in the Central District earns a spot on any short list of things that never disappoint. Each piece pulls its weight, from the soy-soaked tuna and spicy salmon to the furikake-dusted rice and smoky mac salad, and together they add up to something even better.

sen-noodle-bar.blurb: Chinese noodle bowls are the focus at Sen Noodle Bar in Ballard.

seoul-bowl-co.pullQuote: A quick Korean counter on Capitol Hill for a filling bowl at lunch.
seoul-bowl-co.blurb: Korean bowls come over the counter at Seoul Bowl Co, a quick-service stop on Capitol Hill.

serafina.pullQuote: Book the garden patio on a warm night and order a bottle of red.
serafina.blurb: Eastlake's Serafina has been a romantic Italian standby for decades, with a warm, rustic room and a leafy back patio. It's an easy call for an anniversary or a long dinner over pasta and wine.

serious-pie.pullQuote: Order the sausage and peppers pie and grab a seat at the communal tables.
serious-pie.blurb: Pizza night for adults looks like Serious Pie, a Belltown room with an open kitchen, long shared tables, and lighting that's moody but still lets you see your food. Pies come out oval and blistered, with combinations that are inventive without getting silly. The sausage, peppers, and provolone is the standout, and the crust keeps a satisfying chew under its crisp edges.

shaker-spear.pullQuote: Reserve the big round table, order the brûléed mac and cheese, and share.
shaker-spear.blurb: Dinner at Shaker + Spear feels a bit like eating in a very nice home goods showroom, in the best way. The seafood is strong, the staff is sharp and warm, and one round table seats eight if you're bringing a group. Order the prawns in Old Bay butter, the parmesan truffle fries, the charred sprouts, and that torched mac and cheese, then move next door to Pennyroyal for cocktails.

shibuya-hifi.pullQuote: Come for the records and the cocktails, and keep the conversation low.
shibuya-hifi.blurb: Music comes first at Shibuya HiFi, a Ballard listening bar where the sound system and the vinyl get as much attention as the drinks. The cocktails hold up their end, and the night runs long here.

shiro-s-sushi-restaurant.pullQuote: Order both the salmon and tuna samplers, plus a baked crab hand roll.
shiro-s-sushi-restaurant.blurb: A Belltown sushi institution, Shiro's Sushi Restaurant gets everything right, but the samplers are what you will remember. The salmon plate runs through four cuts and preparations, from seared belly to ikura, while the tuna plate shows off lean, marinated, fatty, and negitoro from a single fish. Sit at the counter for omakase at least once, and budget for a special-occasion check.

shomon.pullQuote: Snag a counter seat for eight courses and a crab nugget you'll crave later.
shomon.blurb: From the team behind Shiro's, Shomon gives Seattle omakase a looser, livelier spin. Chefs move around an open kitchen chatting with guests over a mellow lo-fi soundtrack, and the courses mix nigiri with other Japanese small plates, like Hokkaido scallop, futomaki with a soy-cured yolk, and a fried Dungeness crab croquette with béchamel. The counter is roomier than most, and the check lands firmly in special-occasion territory.

shuckers-oyster-bar.pullQuote: Take a bar stool, order a dirty martini, and work through a dozen oysters.
shuckers-oyster-bar.blurb: Inside the Fairmont Olympic, SHUCKERS OYSTER BAR is an old-school room that smells faintly of brine and polished leather. Happy hour knocks the price of local raw oysters way down, and the baked ones topped with toasted brioche and lemony herb butter deserve a spot in your order. The space was a haberdashery in the early twentieth century, and it still has that buttoned-up charm.

single-shot-kitchen-saloon.pullQuote: Order the margherita flatbread and a cocktail for a quiet, easy date.
single-shot-kitchen-saloon.blurb: Few people seem to know about Single Shot Kitchen & Saloon, which gives a date here some built-in novelty. It's a single handsome room, marble bar included, with candles on every table, oddly calm given the noise of Pike-Pine outside. Keep it simple with cocktails and the excellent flatbread, or celebrate with champagne, plenty of small plates, and a good piece of fish.

six-seven-restaurant.pullQuote: Come at sunset, when the view over Elliott Bay does most of the work.
six-seven-restaurant.blurb: Inside the Edgewater Hotel on the waterfront, Six Seven Restaurant is all about the scenery, with big windows and a deck right over the water. The Northwest menu leans on seafood, and happy hour is the low-commitment way to soak it all in.

skalka.pullQuote: Adjaruli khachapuri, a cheese bread boat with a runny yolk, baked to order downtown.
skalka.blurb: Order the Adjaruli and swirl the yolk and butter into the cheese, then tear the crust to dip. Each boat is baked to order in about 15 minutes.

slim-goody.blurb: Bar food and drinks are what you'll find at Slim Goody in Ballard.

snapshot-brewing.blurb: Big groups can spread out over a round of beers at Snapshot Brewing, a brewery in Greenwood.

some-random-bar.pullQuote: Keep this bar in your pocket for dates, groups, and casual catchups alike.
some-random-bar.blurb: Great cocktails, a good crowd, and a menu that runs from burrata to crab nachos make Some Random Bar a dependable Belltown default. There's a patio for warm nights and the bar stays open late. Just warn your friends that it's a real name, not a vague suggestion.

spinasse.pullQuote: Order every pasta you can justify, starting with the buttery tajarin.
spinasse.blurb: For a splurge Italian dinner in Seattle, Spinasse sets the bar, with handmade Piedmontese pasta and service that runs like clockwork. The Capitol Hill dining room mixes reclaimed wood with a sleek marble bar and an open kitchen where you can watch the noodles being made. Expect a special-occasion check, and know the kitchen keeps going late.

guideQuotes.late-night: A late Capitol Hill table is justified once the tajarin hits the bowl.

stampede-cocktail-club.pullQuote: Pair a blueberry mule with dumplings and enjoy the dinosaur staring at you.
stampede-cocktail-club.blurb: At first glance Stampede Cocktail Club reads as a vintage-leaning cocktail bar, until you round a corner and come face to face with a dinosaur head hung against floral wallpaper. The drinks are excellent, including a blueberry mule and a passionfruit margarita with pineapple, and the steamed dumplings come from Little Ting's. It's fun for a date and open late.

star-sushi-bar.blurb: Sushi and drinks are the draw at Star Sushi & Bar on Capitol Hill.

starbucks-coffee-company.pullQuote: Visit once for the history, then drink your daily coffee somewhere quieter.
starbucks-coffee-company.blurb: Tourists line up at the market's Starbucks Coffee Company for the vintage logo and bragging rights to the brand's oldest store. It opens early, so arrive before the crowds if you want the souvenir mug without the wait.

stevie-s-famous.blurb: Pizza is the main event at Stevie's Famous, a casual spot on Beacon Hill.

stoneburner.pullQuote: Skip the pasta, share a few pies, and settle in with a cocktail.
stoneburner.blurb: Neapolitan pizza and pasta share the menu at Stoneburner, but only one of them deserves your attention. Treat it as an upscale pizzeria in Ballard, with drinks, a few appetizers to pass around, and a couple of blistered pies. The dark, handsome room handles dates and group dinners equally well.

storyville-coffee-company.pullQuote: A latte and a Theo chocolate chunk cookie upstairs in the Corner Market building.
storyville-coffee-company.blurb: Order a latte and the chocolate chunk cookie, made with 70% Theo chocolate and Maldon salt. Take the stairs to the top floor at First and Pike.

sugo-hand-roll-bar.pullQuote: Sit at the counter, fill out the card, and order cold sake.
sugo-hand-roll-bar.blurb: Downtown is short on quality sushi lunches, so Sugo Hand Roll Bar at Pike Place fills a real gap with hand rolls built on excellent fish. The four-sided counter looks a bit like an airport bar, yet the room manages to feel calm and lively at once, with blowtorches searing king salmon on a pink salt block. Mark your order on the sheet at your seat and get a carafe of chilled sake.

sunfish.pullQuote: Order the cod and the Greek-spiced fried oysters, and eat by the beach.
sunfish.blurb: Few things say West Seattle like Sunfish, an Alki fish and chips counter that goes dark for most of winter and flips its neon sign back on around February. Squeeze lemon over battered cod that flakes apart and meaty oysters fried with Greek spices for a sunny, casual lunch near the sand.

surrell.pullQuote: Save this Madison Valley tasting menu for a milestone dinner worth dressing up.
surrell.blurb: Surrell builds a multi-course meal around Pacific Northwest ingredients in an intimate Madison Valley room. This is a dressed-up night, best saved for anniversaries and big celebrations.

sushi-by-scratch-restaurants.pullQuote: Book the counter for a parade of nigiri and a seriously special night.
sushi-by-scratch-restaurants.blurb: Sushi by Scratch Restaurants runs an intimate omakase counter in Belltown where chefs work through a long series of creative nigiri right in front of you. It's a special-occasion check, seatings run late, and it's a strong move for impressing visiting parents.

sushi-kappo-tamura.pullQuote: Come for anything from a casual Tuesday to a proposal, and order omakase.
sushi-kappo-tamura.blurb: Eastlake's Sushi Kappo Tamura fits nearly any occasion, from a no-reason weeknight dinner to a big romantic moment. Tables are easier to land here than at the city's other famous sushi counters, and the fish quality is excellent. Sustainability matters, with careful seafood sourcing and produce from the restaurant's own rooftop garden. The chef's tasting menu is a happy choice if you want to hand over the reins.

sushi-kashiba.pullQuote: For the city's best sushi, book the counter and let the chefs decide.
sushi-kashiba.blurb: Skip the waterfront oyster crawl and the fish and chips shops, because the finest seafood in town is at Sushi Kashiba. Shiro Kashiba, who trained under Jiro Ono, opened it at the edge of Pike Place Market in 2015 after leaving his namesake restaurant. Expect impeccable nigiri and a special-occasion check.

sushi-suzuki.pullQuote: Serious omakase without the hush, tucked down an alley in Madison Park.
sushi-suzuki.blurb: Madison Park is all Porsches and pampered dogs, so a back-alley sushi counter fits right in. What surprises is how relaxed Sushi Suzuki feels, a small room squeezed between a bookstore and a salon that could pass for a brewery taproom. The courses are tiny and numerous, the fish does the talking, and the bill is firmly special-occasion.

sweet-alchemy.pullQuote: Get a scoop of Jitter Bars and chase it with something floral.
sweet-alchemy.blurb: Near campus in the U District, Sweet Alchemy scoops flavors you rarely see, like makgeolli, Persian rose, and smoked chocolate, along with mix-ins made from house-baked cakes and cookie dough. The caramel and espresso shortbread flavor called Jitter Bars is the standout, and the shop is open late enough for a post-study treat.

swel-restaurant.blurb: New American cooking is on the menu at SWeL Restaurant in Fremont.

tacos-chukis.pullQuote: Order the adobada tacos with grilled pineapple and you've made the right call.
tacos-chukis.blurb: The Broadway taco counter in a building shared with a tattoo shop stopped being a secret long ago, and Tacos Chukis earned the crowds. The house adobada tacos stack marinated grilled pork with avocado salsa, cilantro, onion, and a seared slab of pineapple. Food comes out quickly, it's cheap, and it's an ideal stop before a night out.

take-5-urban-market.pullQuote: Order the chicken caesar wrap, then come back another day for the reuben.
take-5-urban-market.blurb: Take 5 Urban Market has the Moon Pies and fruit sodas of a proper corner store, plus a short sandwich menu that deserves real attention. The reuben swaps kraut for creamy slaw and gets a crisp layer of griddled swiss, and the sriracha chicken melt brings plenty of avocado and actual heat. Still, the one you will crave is the chicken caesar, packed with bacon, tomato, and crouton bits.

tall-grass-bakery.pullQuote: Organic baguettes, levain and rye, baked in Ballard since 2000.
tall-grass-bakery.blurb: Pick up a classic baguette or the pain au levain, both made with organic flour. The Ballard shop is open Wednesday to Sunday, 9 to 6.

taneda.pullQuote: Book a solo seat for the multi-course kaiseki and sushi meal of your year.
taneda.blurb: Reservations for two at Taneda are nearly impossible, but single seats open up far more often, and a solo dinner here is a treat rather than a consolation. The meal runs around two dozen courses of sushi and kaiseki in a tiny spot at the back of a Capitol Hill indoor mall. The check is a special-occasion one, yet it is a strong value among the city omakase counters.

taste-of-india.pullQuote: Grab a table under the string lights and order the fish coconut curry.
taste-of-india.blurb: A giant pergola strung with lights shelters the outdoor seating at Taste of India, which feels more like a mellow backyard than a U District restaurant. Free potato and pea samosas land soon after you sit, and the long menu moves fast. Get the tandoori wings, butter chicken, and shimla paneer, but save room for the coconut fish curry, which is impossibly tender.

tat-s-delicatessen.pullQuote: Philly cheesesteak or pastrami are both hits here, and it might be the best cheesesteak in the city.
tat-s-delicatessen.blurb: Philly cheesesteak or pastrami are both hits here, and it might be the best cheesesteak in the city.

taurus-ox.pullQuote: Bring the parents for Lao food that feels comforting and still like a real night out.
taurus-ox.blurb: Capitol Hill's Taurus Ox cooks Lao food with real heat and funk, and it rewards a table that's willing to share. Order sticky rice no matter what. The room works as well for a date as it does for dinner with your folks.

taylor-shellfish-farms.pullQuote: Order raw oysters by the dozen and grab the wall tables if you brought a date.
taylor-shellfish-farms.blurb: Taylor Shellfish Farms has been growing oysters in Washington for well over a century, and this Pioneer Square bar puts that harvest on ice. Branch out with Dungeness crab or Manila clams once the first round is gone. Couples should claim the tables along the wall, and the bar is there when you would rather face the shells than each other. Happy hour makes a second round easier to justify.

temple-pastries.pullQuote: Get the caramelized shallot croissant first, then let the pastry case talk you into more.
temple-pastries.blurb: The pastries at Temple Pastries look almost too pretty to eat, though you'll get over that fast. Start with the croissant packed with jammy shallots and gruyere, then add a pistachio schnecken or a blood orange Campari cake donut. A few macarons for later never hurt, and nothing in this early-opening Central District bakery will dent your wallet.

terra-plata.pullQuote: Rooftop brunch here is worth a sunburn, so bring sunscreen and a big appetite.
terra-plata.blurb: Terra Plata's rooftop garden on Capitol Hill turns brunch into a long, sunny affair, with a Spanish-leaning breakfast that kicks off nicely with patatas bravas. The roof gets brutally hot in summer, so plan accordingly. Come back around sunset for wine and snacks, which is when the waffled potato chips with truffle salt appear. It also makes a strong date spot.

that-s-amore-italian-cafe.pullQuote: Rigatoni Bolognese and bucatini carbonara with a skyline-to-Olympics view in Mount Baker.
that-s-amore-italian-cafe.blurb: Order the rigatoni Bolognese or the bucatini carbonara, and ask for a table facing the view. Clear evenings reach the Olympics.

the-alley.pullQuote: Walk through a locker door into a velvet cocktail lounge hiding behind a Vietnamese restaurant.
the-alley.blurb: The Alley hides behind Bonjour Vietnam, a sleepy West Seattle restaurant, past what looks like a storage room stacked with booster seats and coolers. Open the right locker and you land in a plush bar of crystal chandeliers and velvet stools, with liquor locked inside glass cabinets. Order the jungle punch with cajun wings from the kitchen up front. Live jazz plays Sunday and Monday nights, and the bar keeps going late.

the-angry-beaver.pullQuote: Come for hockey on every screen and a plate of poutine for the table.
the-angry-beaver.blurb: Hockey is always on at The Angry Beaver, a Greenwood sports bar where poutine is the move. It handles big groups without fuss.

the-boat.pullQuote: Order the garlic fried chicken rice and eat lunch aboard a landlocked wooden ship.
the-boat.blurb: Docked in a parking lot in the International District, The Boat is a wooden ship the Phở Bắc team brought back to life in 2022. The main reason to climb aboard is the fried Cornish hen over rice, slicked with garlicky fish sauce. Think of it as a quick, unfussy lunch that doesn't require much planning.

the-brim-coffee-shop.pullQuote: Cheap, early coffee in Belltown, plus a rooftop to drink it on.
the-brim-coffee-shop.blurb: Early risers in Belltown can grab inexpensive coffee at The Brim Coffee Shop, which also has a rooftop for sipping it.

the-butcher-s-table.pullQuote: Mishima Reserve Wagyu steaks from the Beecher's family.
the-butcher-s-table.blurb: Order a Mishima Reserve American Wagyu steak. The company that raises the beef also owns Beecher's, and a butcher case sells the same cuts.

the-capital-grille.pullQuote: A classic special-occasion steakhouse for impressing your parents, ideally on their dime.
the-capital-grille.blurb: Downtown, The Capital Grille sticks to the dark-wood steakhouse formula with a big check and the polish that parents tend to appreciate.

the-carlile-room.pullQuote: Book it before a show when you want a stylish dinner steps from the theater.
the-carlile-room.blurb: Across from the Paramount Theatre, The Carlile Room serves New American plates in a colorful downtown room that's handy for pre-show meals.

the-chicken-supply.pullQuote: This gluten-free Filipino fried chicken is crispier than nearly anything else in town.
the-chicken-supply.blurb: The Chicken Supply dredges its Filipino fried chicken in tapioca, rice flour, and potato starch, and that celiac-friendly coating is exactly why it's so good. Thigh skin crackles like a chip, and the skewers of white meat stay remarkably juicy. Seating is limited to a handful of tables in the small Phinney Ridge room. Prices stay pleasantly low.

the-corson-building.pullQuote: Save this Georgetown garden house for an anniversary dinner you'll talk about for years.
the-corson-building.blurb: Set inside an early twentieth-century house in Georgetown, The Corson Building glows with candles and vintage decor, and the garden terrace has wood nymph statues. It's only open Thursday through Sunday, with à la carte dinners at the start of the stretch and prix fixe on weekends. Expect a special-occasion check and make a reservation.

the-crumpet-shop.pullQuote: A warm crumpet with ricotta and pesto beats every other quick breakfast at the market.
the-crumpet-shop.blurb: Breakfast options at Pike Place Market are thin, which makes The Crumpet Shop so useful. The crumpets are springy and crisp, and their little holes trap toppings like pesto with ricotta or raspberry preserves. Be there while the crumpets are still warm and hardly anything is spent.

the-diller-room.pullQuote: Grab a marble barstool under the neon glow and order something classic.
the-diller-room.blurb: The Diller Room has been pouring drinks in some form for more than a hundred years, which puts it ahead of the Space Needle. At night the marble bar picks up light from the old Diller Hotel neon sign, and the menu mixes old standards with modern cocktails. The crowd is friendly and very Seattle.

the-doctor-s-office.pullQuote: Tell the bartender your mood and let them write you a cocktail prescription.
the-doctor-s-office.blurb: Drinks at The Doctor's Office feel like a generous friend is mixing them in their living room. You might be greeted with a splash of Champagne, and the small, dark room holds just a sofa and a marble bar. The menu takes some decoding, so describe what you want and trust the staff. You should book a reservation.

the-dressing-room.pullQuote: A late-night Pike Place stop for a cocktail or a glass of wine.
the-dressing-room.blurb: Near Pike Place Market, The Dressing Room pours cocktails and wine until late.

the-flora-bakehouse.pullQuote: Take your almond croissant up to the rooftop and call it an afternoon.
the-flora-bakehouse.blurb: Up on a second floor in Beacon Hill, The Flora Bakehouse fills its case with cheddar-chive scones, fudgy vegan brownies, and twice-baked almond croissants that shatter everywhere. The real bonus is the U-shaped rooftop, which turns an iced cardamom rose latte or a soft serve into a lazy afternoon. Beacon Hill can get a scone before the neighborhood alarm clocks go off.

the-flour-box.pullQuote: The brioche donuts justify showing up two hours early with a camp chair.
the-flour-box.blurb: People line up outside The Flour Box well before the doors open, and the brioche donuts explain why. Flavors rotate constantly, from torched crème brûlée to savory everything-spiced cream cheese, Oreo mascarpone, or Thai tea. If the Basque cheesecake is around, get it. The shop sits in Hillman City, just south of Columbia City.

the-fonte-bar.pullQuote: A downtown cocktail bar that's already open when most bars are still asleep.
the-fonte-bar.blurb: Downtown, The Fonté Bar mixes pricier cocktails and opens its doors early in the day.

the-french-guys.pullQuote: Order the plain croissant, a steady classic that gets every essential right.
the-french-guys.blurb: The French Guys works out of a little stone cottage on Capitol Hill that looks lifted from a storybook. Their plain croissant isn't the flakiest or richest around, but it's buttery, crunchy, and dependable in a way you'll come to count on. It opens early, and prices are gentle.

the-george.pullQuote: Dress up, sit at the bar, and order the lamb agnolotti with fries.
the-george.blurb: The George brings real glamour to the renovated Fairmont Olympic Hotel, and it's somewhere you can dress up without feeling silly. The menu runs long, from seafood towers to pasta, and not all of it lands, so skip the steak and duck. Go for lamb agnolotti in parmesan broth and a side of fries with some bubbles. Expect a special-occasion bill.

the-hart-and-the-hunter.pullQuote: An early-opening downtown spot for an American breakfast before a busy day.
the-hart-and-the-hunter.blurb: Downtown's The Hart and The Hunter serves American food starting before the street is busy.

the-harvest-vine.pullQuote: Head downstairs to the candlelit wine cellar for the most romantic tapas in town.
the-harvest-vine.blurb: The Harvest Vine looks modest from the street in Madison Valley, but the stone wine cellar downstairs, lit by candles and lined with dusty Tempranillo, does the romantic work for you. Order olives, jamón, a wedge of tortilla española, and the sherry-soaked mushrooms. Servers mostly leave you alone, and the place also works for a group sharing tapas.

the-little-beast.pullQuote: Get the korma pie and accept every extra pour of gravy offered.
the-little-beast.blurb: From the folks behind Beast & Cleaver, The Little Beast looks like a regular British pub on Ballard's main drag until the food arrives. The lamb korma pie comes buried in gravy, the currywurst sausage roll pairs well with a Pimm's cup, and the charred pork chop with grilled nectarines is a standout. Scotch eggs and sing-along rock round out the evening.

the-nest.pullQuote: Rooftop cocktails and smoked salmon dip above Pike Place at the Thompson Hotel.
the-nest.blurb: Order a Seattle After Dark, with brown butter-washed rye and rum, and the smoked salmon dip. Expect a 20% service charge.

the-other-coast-cafe.pullQuote: East-coast deli on Ballard Ave. Get the Electric Wizard or Rajun Cajun.
the-other-coast-cafe.blurb: East-coast deli on Ballard Ave. Get the Electric Wizard or Rajun Cajun.

the-pastry-project.pullQuote: In summer, get the soft serve buried under rainbow peanut crunch.
the-pastry-project.blurb: The Pastry Project is a training program for bakers, and in warm months its front door becomes a soft serve window. Even plain vanilla and chocolate get exciting with the rainbow peanut topping, which tastes like a Butterfinger without the sticky aftermath. Colder months bring cinnamon rolls and gooey chocolate chip cookies from the same Pioneer Square window.

the-pink-door.pullQuote: Go for the lasagna and the cabaret, and fight for a seat on the deck.
the-pink-door.blurb: Behind an unmarked pink door in Post Alley, The Pink Door has paired Italian-American comfort food with trapeze acts and cabaret for decades. The summer deck looks out over Elliott Bay, and lasagna is the order. It works for a date, a visiting friend, or a late dinner near Pike Place Market.

guideQuotes.rooftops: The deck over the market is the prize, lasagna merely the excuse to sit.
guideQuotes.restaurants-with-a-view: The deck over the market is the prize, lasagna merely the excuse to sit.

the-shambles.pullQuote: Start with the wagyu bavette and never skip the mushrooms with jammy egg yolk.
the-shambles.blurb: With its dive-bar look and stiff cocktails, The Shambles in Roosevelt doesn't advertise that it's a top-tier steakhouse. A chalkboard lists the cuts, and the wagyu bavette arrives crusty, rosy, and pooled with demiglace. Charred broccolini in a sharp Dijon sauce and creamy herbed mushrooms are just as essential. It works well for dinner with your parents.

the-shop-by-porter.pullQuote: A cheap, early-opening downtown cafe for coffee before work.
the-shop-by-porter.blurb: Downtown coffee from The Shop by Porter starts early in the morning and won't cost much.

the-sitting-room.pullQuote: Pick the back sofas for friends or a candlelit table for a date.
the-sitting-room.blurb: Dim and friendly, The Sitting Room is where you sip spritzes and work through olives and truffled almonds. Potato chips with house onion dip could easily be dinner. Sofas fill the back, the bar has a library-desk feel, and the row of candlelit tables suits a date.

the-traveling-goat.pullQuote: A low-key Lower Queen Anne cocktail bar for a drink near Seattle Center.
the-traveling-goat.blurb: In Lower Queen Anne, The Traveling Goat mixes cocktails at friendly prices.

the-usual.pullQuote: Order a latte with the chicken pelmeni and you'll understand the hype.
the-usual.blurb: The Usual looks like any coffee shop on the ground floor of a new apartment building, complete with croissants and latte art. The surprise is the Eastern European dumplings, like dill-brightened chicken pelmeni and potato vareniki topped with bacon. Paired with espresso on a cold Central District morning, they hit hard.

the-walrus-and-the-carpenter.pullQuote: Come before sunset, sit at the marble bar, and order oysters by the dozen.
the-walrus-and-the-carpenter.blurb: The Walrus and The Carpenter draws an oyster line in Ballard even though the bay is nowhere in sight. The room feels like a farmhouse that traded livestock for shellfish, and it shines in late afternoon when sunlight bounces off the mirrors. Happy hour helps, and a date here rarely goes wrong.

the-wayland-mill.pullQuote: Bring a book for breakfast or five friends for dinner, and always get the canele.
the-wayland-mill.blurb: Japanese cooking with a Midwestern diner attitude is the deal at The Wayland Mill, a big, bright Wallingford space near the water. Mornings bring scallion biscuits with miso gravy, and the canele is excellent. Later, clarified cocktails and a serious wine list take over, and service stays quick whether you're alone or with a crowd.

the-white-swan-public-house.pullQuote: Skip the sunny-afternoon crowds and come after dark for the lit-up lake.
the-white-swan-public-house.blurb: Nautical decor and big water views make The White Swan Public House look like a tourist trap, but it mostly sidesteps the clichés. Stick with the seafood and you'll eat well. Warm afternoons get packed, so come after sundown, when tables open up and party boats drift across Lake Union. Happy hour and big groups are both easy here.

three-girls-bakery.pullQuote: Do not leave without the giant shortbread cookie crowned with fudge.
three-girls-bakery.blurb: It's really just a long glass case and a register in Pike Place Market, but everything inside Three Girls Bakery is good. Look for the oversized m&m cookie, the peanut butter cookie hiding a whole Reese's cup, and the raspberry crumble bar. The fudge-topped shortbread dot is mandatory. For lunch, the counter next door makes a salmon salad sandwich.

tilikum-place-cafe.pullQuote: Book ahead for the potato waffle benedict, and let someone else order the dutch baby.
tilikum-place-cafe.blurb: Puffy, sugar-dusted dutch babies made Tilikum Place Café a Belltown brunch fixture, but the supporting cast is the real draw. Think thick-cut bacon, smoked salmon benedict on potato waffles, and bubbling egg skillets layered with gruyere. The small room fills as soon as the doors open, so reserve a table.

tivoli.pullQuote: Treat the pizza as a side and load up on focaccia and cold noodles.
tivoli.blurb: Tivoli comes from the crews behind Post Alley Pizza and Saint Bread, and the pies at this Fremont spot are excellent. Still, the smart move is building a meal around everything else, like focaccia with tomato nori butter, Philly tomato pie under house ricotta, and chilled noodles in pistachio butter and chili crisp. Share one pizza among four and fill in the rest.

toasted-bagels-coffee.pullQuote: An early, inexpensive U District stop for a bagel before class.
toasted-bagels-coffee.blurb: Bagels and coffee at TOASTED Bagels & Coffee start early in the U District, and prices stay low.

top-pot-doughnuts.pullQuote: Crackly old-fashioned doughnuts under floor-to-ceiling bookshelves at Top Pot's Fifth Avenue flagship.
top-pot-doughnuts.blurb: Get an old-fashioned, then a pink Feather Boa, and grab a seat by the tall shelves. The Belltown flagship is the one to visit.

toulouse-petit.pullQuote: Order the BBQ shrimp with grits and bring the whole birthday crew.
toulouse-petit.blurb: Stick with Creole standbys at Toulouse Petit, like barbecue shrimp over grits or a bowl of seafood gumbo, and you'll leave happy. The antique-feeling Lower Queen Anne dining room hums with energy, which makes it great for birthdays and anniversaries. Brunch starts early, happy hour is popular.

triangle-spirits-fremont.pullQuote: Come for the fried chicken sandwich and stay for a coupe cocktail.
triangle-spirits-fremont.blurb: Inside what looks like a wood-paneled Fremont dive, Triangle Spirits Fremont makes a chicken sandwich that rivals anyone's, with a crackly crust, juicy breast meat, and just lettuce, pickles, and mayo. The cheeseburger with American cheese and relish-heavy sauce is just as strong. Add fries or gravy-soaked mashed potatoes and you've got a real dinner, not just drinks.

tulio.pullQuote: A dependable downtown Italian dining room for pasta before a night out.
tulio.blurb: Downtown's Tulio has been serving Italian food out of the Hotel Vintage for decades, and pasta is the draw.

umi-sake-house.pullQuote: Book the back room for a date fueled by salmon nigiri and sake.
umi-sake-house.blurb: Before Momiji, there was Umi Sake House, and the first one is still the pick. Ask for the back dining room, which feels like a bamboo garden turned lounge, and order a nigiri sampler plus rolls with seared snow crab or spicy yellowtail. Big groups can usually book even the night before, and the happy hour and late kitchen help.

guideQuotes.happy-hour: The late pour is the excuse, and the salmon nigiri is why anyone stays.

un-bien.pullQuote: The Caribbean roast. Best sandwich in Seattle. Garlic sauce, pork, and that bread. Don't order anything else.
un-bien.blurb: The Caribbean roast. Best sandwich in Seattle. Garlic sauce, pork, and that bread. Don't order anything else.

un-po-tipsy.pullQuote: A casual Pioneer Square pizza stop that holds its own among better pies.
un-po-tipsy.blurb: Pioneer Square has a solid pizza option in Un Po Tipsy, where prices stay moderate.

uneeda-burger.pullQuote: A no-fuss Fremont counter for a cheap burger without a reservation.
uneeda-burger.blurb: Walk in, order at the counter, and Uneeda Burger will hand you an inexpensive burger in Fremont.

unlisted.pullQuote: Order the Eléphante 75 and toast the giant elephant in the corner.
unlisted.blurb: Unlisted hides behind an unmarked alley door inside The Ruins, an event venue in Queen Anne. Dark wood, velvet, a huge elephant statue, and diamond-shaped chandeliers set a moody scene. The cocktails, like the citrusy Sideshow and the Champagne-topped Eléphante 75, are carefully made. Good bars are scarce in this neighborhood, which helps it stand out.

url-coffee.pullQuote: Order a Walk To Work latte and settle into the calmest workspace in First Hill.
url-coffee.blurb: URL Coffee looks more like a furniture showroom than a cafe, with natural wood and paper lanterns everywhere. It's a relaxing place to work if you can grab a seat at the long table or one of the small ones. Whatever you do, get the Walk To Work, an iced latte under cinnamon whipped cream.

valentina-s-cafe.pullQuote: An early Ballard coffee stop for your first cup of the day.
valentina-s-cafe.blurb: Valentina’s Cafe pours coffee in Ballard from early morning on.

valhalla-sandwiches.pullQuote: Order the Thanksgiving turkey sandwich and add tater tots for dunking.
valhalla-sandwiches.blurb: Valhalla Sandwiches in Greenwood manages to go big without getting sloppy. The sandwiches come on sturdy telera rolls with fillings like blackened shrimp and chorizo, chicken with sweet-hot mustard and slaw, or turkey with stuffing, cranberry, and rosemary aioli. Tater tots with chipotle mayo are a must, and the whole thing is inexpensive.

vendemmia.pullQuote: Hide out here with a bowl of pasta and a good bottle of wine.
vendemmia.blurb: Opened by the people behind Le Messe, Vendemmia is a quiet Madrona escape built around pasta and wine. Pick a bottle, then choose between spaghetti with tomato and chili or taleggio-filled agnolotti. Expect a special-occasion bill, and treat it as a reliable date night.

victrola-coffee-roasters.pullQuote: Bring the laptop and grab a spot at the big communal table.
victrola-coffee-roasters.blurb: Victrola Coffee Roasters on Capitol Hill has strong espresso, a steady hum of people working, and a communal table roomy enough for your laptop and a giant mug. It's also air-conditioned, which matters during a summer heat wave. Their iced vanilla latte is great.

vindicktive-wings.pullQuote: Come for the wings, stay for the chaos, and catch the game if you must.
vindicktive-wings.blurb: Vindicktive Wings looks like a generic Belltown sports bar at first, all big booths and TVs, but people show up here for wings first and the game second. Give it time and the room starts to feel like a great college party, with loud music and bartenders who remember you. The wings are inexpensive.

volunteer-park-cafe-pantry.pullQuote: Order the BEC on a poppy roll, then grab a pastry for later.
volunteer-park-cafe-pantry.blurb: Tucked into a house in north Capitol Hill, Volunteer Park Cafe & Pantry would be worth a visit for pastries alone, like tahini caramel bars and buckwheat chocolate chunk cookies. The breakfast sandwich is the real star, with thin folded eggs, barely crisp bacon, and melty American cheese on a toasted house poppy seed roll. Laptops aren't allowed on weekends.

von-s-1000spirits.pullQuote: Use it for happy hour and stick around for the hourly drink wheel.
von-s-1000spirits.blurb: Von's 1000Spirits lives up to its name with a huge bar and a long list of bottles. The sourdough pizza and pasta are solid and the cocktails are better, but this is mostly a happy hour or post-day-drinking lunch move. Every hour they spin a wheel to pick the drink special, and it stays open late.

voodoo-doughnut.pullQuote: Bacon maple bars and pretzel-staked Voodoo Dolls, open late on Capitol Hill's Pine Street.
voodoo-doughnut.blurb: Order the bacon maple bar, the Portland chain's famous one, and a raspberry-filled Voodoo Doll. It's open until 11 or midnight daily.

w-living-room-bar.pullQuote: A sleek downtown hotel lounge for a late cocktail after dinner.
w-living-room-bar.blurb: Inside the downtown W hotel, W Living Room Bar pours pricier cocktails late into the night.

wa-z.pullQuote: Save the kaiseki menu for an occasion, and savor the sushi courses most.
wa-z.blurb: Near the Space Needle, where most restaurants disappoint, wa'z quietly serves an excellent kaiseki menu on beautiful dinnerware. The eight courses change monthly but usually include soup, a generous piece of wagyu, and terrific sushi, often brightened with yuzu and mirin. Flavors lean subtle rather than flashy. It's a special-occasion check.

wasabi-sushi-izakaya.pullQuote: A late Belltown sushi spot with a happy hour worth planning around.
wasabi-sushi-izakaya.blurb: Belltown's Wasabi Sushi & Izakaya serves sushi and izakaya plates late into the night, and the discounted hour is a strong reason to stop in.

wataru-sushi-restaurant.pullQuote: Wear flannel, grab a table for two, and order the seared black cod.
wataru-sushi-restaurant.blurb: WATARU Sushi Restaurant in Ravenna is a dressy-casual date spot where flannel fits right in, even though prices run high. Nigiri highlights include Hokkaido scallop with bamboo salt and lightly seared black cod. The omakase counter is tough to book, but tables come with set dinners and great starters like a fish cake slider on lotus root buns.

west-of-chicago-pizza-company.pullQuote: Neon cheese, Italian beef, and great pizza will make homesick Chicagoans very happy.
west-of-chicago-pizza-company.blurb: With ramekins of neon-orange cheese, red plastic cups for soda, and the smell of Italian beef in the air, West of Chicago Pizza Company could pass for a suburban Chicago joint. The pizza is genuinely great, Chicagoan or not. It works for a group dinner or a laid-back date in West Seattle.

wet-clay-cafe.pullQuote: An early, inexpensive Fremont cafe for a morning coffee stop.
wet-clay-cafe.blurb: Wet Clay Cafe opens early in Fremont and keeps its prices low.

wild-fish-poke.pullQuote: Grab a poke bowl at the market when you need a quick lunch.
wild-fish-poke.blurb: At Pike Place Market, Wild Fish Poke serves Hawaiian-style poke from a counter.

wild-ginger-kitchen.pullQuote: A polished downtown pick for pan-Asian plates before a show or meeting.
wild-ginger-kitchen.blurb: Wild Ginger Kitchen serves Asian fusion dishes in a polished downtown dining room.

willmott-s-ghost.pullQuote: Book the Spheres room when a Roman pizza night should feel like a splurge.
willmott-s-ghost.blurb: Renee Erickson's Willmott's Ghost sits inside the Amazon Spheres, a blush-pink room serving Roman-inspired Italian food. Order the Roman-style pizza and pastas, and plan on a special-occasion check.

windy-city-pie.pullQuote: Order the deep dish and fight over the caramelized cheese edge.
windy-city-pie.blurb: Phinney Ridge gets serious deep-dish pizza from Windy City Pie, where a crispy, caramelized cheese crust rings every pan.

wood-shop-bbq.pullQuote: Get the ribs, plus whatever else your finger happens to land on.
wood-shop-bbq.blurb: Wood Shop BBQ started as a food truck and now runs a Central District restaurant with a patio, and its smoked meats rank with the best in town. Brisket, brined chicken thigh, pulled pork sandwiches, and even portobello machaca on brioche are all safe bets. Save room for the ribs, which are the main event.

young-s-restaurant.pullQuote: Order Mickey Mouse pancakes and Mongolian beef at the same table.
young-s-restaurant.blurb: Out in White Center, Young's Restaurant serves American diner breakfasts alongside a long list of Chinese and Thai dishes. Picture deep booths, checkered floors, and little creamer cups on every table. It's ideal on a Sunday morning when nobody agrees, since one person can get an omelette with hash browns while another orders garlic fried chicken and crab rangoons.

zig-zag-cafe.pullQuote: Order a classic cocktail and the lamb pastitsio, then share a booth.
zig-zag-cafe.blurb: Zig Zag Café is known for cocktails, but skipping the Greek food here would be a mistake. Go for the lamb pastitsio, marinated chicken kebabs with a side of tzatziki, and a sesame-rich hummus. Booths force you onto the same side. It stays open late, and happy hour is a classic.

tendon-kohaku.pullQuote: Black truffle carbonara udon with bacon, egg yolk and Parmesan.
tendon-kohaku.blurb: Come for the black truffle carbonara udon: Parmesan cream, bacon, black pepper and an egg yolk. The tempura bowls over rice can come second.

catch.pullQuote: Truffle sashimi and the Catch Roll under a retractable roof.
catch.blurb: Start with the truffle sashimi: tuna and hamachi, chili ponzu, black truffle purée and Kaluga caviar. The rooftop looks out to the Hollywood Hills.

la-mar-bellevue.pullQuote: Gastón Acurio's cebiche bar, on Main Street in Bellevue.
la-mar-bellevue.blurb: Order cebiche first, like the Cebiche Nissei from the cebiche bar, then lomo saltado. It's Acurio's first Northwest restaurant.

ascend-prime-steak-and-sushi.pullQuote: A5 wagyu and omakase, 31 floors above Bellevue.
ascend-prime-steak-and-sushi.blurb: Come for the wagyu: Miyazaki A5 filet by the ounce, or a three-cut tenderloin flight in the lounge. The sushi bar runs a premium omakase.

daniels-broiler.pullQuote: Prime filet on the 21st floor, Bellevue's steakhouse since 1989.
daniels-broiler.blurb: Order the Daniel's Cut, a 12-ounce Prime filet under the house steak butter. The decks face the Seattle skyline and the Olympics.

cantina-monarca.pullQuote: Handmade-tortilla tacos and over 100 tequilas in Bellevue.
cantina-monarca.blurb: Get the Baja sea bass taco, battered and fried with apple slaw, and a pork belly taco next to it. The tequila list runs past 100 bottles.

carmines.pullQuote: Il Terrazzo Carmine's veal scaloppine, by Downtown Park.
carmines.blurb: Order the veal scaloppine with lemon and capers, the family's Il Terrazzo classic. The glass wall opens onto a patio facing Downtown Park.

minamoto.pullQuote: Seasonal omakase from New York's Iki alumni, in Bellevue.
minamoto.blurb: Book the omakase: 15 to 18 seasonal courses at two seatings, reserved at least three days ahead. The regular menu covers sushi, tempura and wagyu.

water-grill-bellevue.pullQuote: Live Dungeness crab by the pound and a raw bar on Bellevue Way.
water-grill-bellevue.blurb: In season, order the live Washington Dungeness, steamed and sold by the pound. Start at the raw bar, and expect the menu to change daily with the catch.

limoncello.pullQuote: Stacked Italian deli sandwiches on Sutter Street.
limoncello.blurb: Order the Siciliano: ham, salami and pistachio mortadella with provolone and pepperoncini. There's pizza and an Italian grocery shelf too.

republique.pullQuote: The Manzkes' bakery and bistro in Chaplin's 1929 building.
